metadata.title: Awesome Tactile Hands
metadata.scope: Public datasets that record touch across the hand during manipulation: human tactile gloves and dexterous robot hands with tactile sensing.

datasets.name: TouchScale
datasets.title: TouchScale: 500 Hours of Human Vision and Touch for Visual-Tactile Learning
datasets.summary: Bimanual tactile gloves with 880 taxels per hand (normal force in N plus two tangential components per taxel), recorded with a head-mounted RGB-D camera and two wrist cameras; the released 100 h cover 929 tasks in 22 scene types.
datasets.hand: Tachin glove x 2 (episode files name it Tujian EI-G012)

sensor.note: 15 pads per hand stored as tactile_<k> (T, rows, cols), normal force per taxel in N: thumb tip 16x10, thumb middle 4x8, thenar 13x8; index, middle and ring 9x8 + 3x8 + 4x8; little 9x8 + 3x8; hypothenar 13x8. Every taxel also has tf_tactile_x / tf_tactile_y tangential components (unit not stated). Per-sample Unix timestamps; the per-episode rate is 30-100 Hz (metadata glove_rate_hz). 1.5 x 1.5 mm cells, spatial resolution below 2 mm (paper).

scale.text: 100 h released of 500 h planned: 15,324 episodes, 929 tasks, 22 scene types, 905+ objects, 24 participants (paper, full 500 h: ~87K episodes, ~2K tasks, 1.5K+ objects, ~20 participants)

datasets.access: Gated on Hugging Face with automatic approval (log in and agree to share username and email). 100 h are released as 430 WebDataset tar shards (1.06 TB), per-episode preview videos (26 GB) and 193 object meshes (2.3 GB); the full 500 h is planned before November 2026.
caveats: No hand-pose files; the paper estimates pose with WiLoR.
Each episode's 17 files sit inside a ~2.5 GB tar shard; fetching one episode needs range reads over the tar headers or the whole shard.
Glove rate differs by session (30-100 Hz); the card says to use the per-sample timestamps. The glove's 8-bit frame counter skips values in most sessions, which the release does not explain.
Tactile unit: the card calls the values the glove's calibrated output in newtons; episode.h5 marks them 'newton_assumed_from_vendor_calibrated_output'. Tangential components have no stated unit.
Participants are predominantly male (95 of 15,324 episodes by female participants, per the card).

cameras.resolution: 1280x720 RGB; depth 640x480 native (paper), released registered to the RGB at 1280x720, 16-bit mm

tracking.note: Paper runs WiLoR on auto-detected hand crops for its experiments; no pose file in the release and no hand-tracking hardware.

other: head IMU (accelerometer m/s^2 + gyroscope rad/s, ~200 Hz, Orbbec Gemini 345Lg)
per-taxel tangential components (tf_tactile_x / tf_tactile_y)
English instruction, task name, object list and leading hand per episode
193 textured object meshes (Meshy reconstructions, scale not metric)
camera intrinsics, Kalibr RGB/depth/IMU calibration and per-episode glove calibration tables
per-episode preview video (960x540, 12 fps) with all streams composited

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/2077AIDataFoundation/TouchScale/blob/74914cc2e11d0a7f37ddbe5d57db4fe4e14a0a7e/README.md (read with HF auth, revision 74914cc, last modified 2026-10-23)
https://huggingface.co/datasets/2077AIDataFoundation/TouchScale file listing via the HF API at 74914cc: 16,353 files, 1.085 TB
https://huggingface.co/datasets/2077AIDataFoundation/TouchScale dataset page (gate text, read without login)

All 17 files of 9 episodes opened: shards data/train-00000, -00032, -00083, -00204, -00406, -00422 and -00429 of 430 (byte-range reads), plus previews/train/000/5a1ae97d-9456-479a-8a4e-4cd6c7f07773.mp4
https://huggingface.co/datasets/2077AIDataFoundation/TouchScale-OXT (dataset page and HF API metadata, read without login, 2026-10-25)
unconfirmed: Maker: episode.h5 metadata attribute source_dataset reads 'Orbbec Gemini 345Lg; Intel RealSense D405; Tujian EI-G012'. Tujian is the pinyin of 途见 (Tachin Technology), whose EI-G series is the TachinGlove on tachin.com; the paper names only the 'Tachin Glove'. Paper: 'The data are purchased by Overfit Lab and captured by Noitom under our contracted data-collection process.'
hours=100.0 is the sum of duration_s and frames=10,800,039 the sum of num_frames (head camera, 30 fps) over metadata/episodes.parquet; the card says 100.0 h.
tasks=929 is the card's count; episodes.parquet has 953 distinct task_id and 920 distinct task_name values.

rate_hz 30-100: glove_rate_hz in episodes.parquet runs from 30.0 to 99.8 Hz (6,850 episodes at 35 Hz, 1,836 near 57 Hz, the rest 39-100 Hz). The card says 35-90 Hz and 'about 35, 57 or 65-90 Hz'; the paper gives 50 Hz over WiFi and 100 Hz over USB.

Glove frame counter (8-bit frame_numbers) in the 9 opened episodes: the 57 Hz session advances by 1 per stored sample; 35 Hz sessions advance by 1 or 2 alternately at even 28.6 ms steps; 53-91 Hz sessions store 10 ms steps with 20-62 ms gaps where the counter jumps by 2-4 (6-30% of counter values absent). Whether these are dropped packets is not stated.

Tangential components: unit not stated; the geometry file gives per-taxel dir_x / dir_y axes but does not say tf_tactile_x / _y follow them. The median ratio of tangential magnitude to normal force (taxels above 0.2 N) is 0.02-2.3% per glove file in the 8 sampled episodes.

calibrated=true rests on the card ('the glove's calibrated output in newtons') and the per-episode glove_<side>_calib.json (7 parts, each a 20-point nonlinearity curve and 1,024 gain pairs); episode.h5 marks the unit as assumed.

Positions that never read: in the 18 glove files opened, 116 of 880 positions never exceed 0.05 N in either glove, among them the same fingertip-end positions in every finger (distal pad row 8 columns 2-5, row 7 columns 1, 2 and 6) and most of the thumb tip pad's last four rows. The layout figure draws all 880; whether these positions sense is not stated.
Depth resolution: paper 640x480 native; the release's depth_head.mkv is 1280x720 FFV1 gray16le registered to the head RGB (kalibr T_depth_cam is identity).
subjects: the paper says about 20 participants for 500 h; the release card and episodes.parquet give 24 pseudonymous actor ids.
objects=905 is the card's '905+'; 193 of them have meshes.
scene_types are the 7 environment words of the card; scenes=22 counts the scene field of episodes.parquet (the paper's 9 high-level settings refer to the full 500 h).
imu.txt header says '#timestamp[ns]' but the first column holds Unix seconds (e.g. 1788249254.095250); measured rate 201.7-203.0 Hz in the 8 sampled episodes.

rank.label: Apply for access
why: download after an application: Hugging Face gate, automatic approval
8 sample episodes opened in the viewer

faults.text: The glove's 8-bit frame_numbers counter skips values between stored samples in 7 of 8 episodes (6-38% of counter values per glove file; only the 57 Hz session advances by 1 every sample). 35 Hz sessions step evenly (28.6 ms); in the 53-91 Hz sessions 3-15% of steps are longer than twice the median, the longest 62 ms. The release does not say whether skipped values are dropped packets; if they are, more than 5% of glove frames are missing in those 7 episodes.

Taxels at 0 N for the whole episode while their 4 neighbours averaged above 0.2 N for over 1 s: 0-17 per glove file (at most 17 of 880 = 1.9%, kettle right glove and unscrew left glove). Named per episode in the viewer notes.

Taxels holding a maximum above 1 N exactly for over 0.5 s (flat top): 0-6 per glove file (unscrew left glove 6, tape-dispenser right glove 4); at most 0.25% of the shown values (kettle left glove) reach the 1.5 N colour limit.

116 of 880 positions never exceed 0.05 N in either glove across the 18 glove files opened, including the same fingertip-end positions in every finger and most of the thumb tip pad's last four rows (about 66 positions, 7.5%). They may be untouched or non-sensing; the release counts all 880 as taxels and does not say.
One head-camera step of 67 ms (one missing frame) in the peel episode (82a95f58); the depth stream has the same gap. Every other camera step in the sample is 33-34 ms.

datasets.name: EgoTouch
datasets.title: TouchAnything: A Dataset and Framework for Bimanual Tactile Estimation from Egocentric Video
datasets.summary: Bimanual pressure gloves with Rokoko finger tracking and Vive wrist trackers, a chest camera and two fisheye wrist cameras, 208 tasks in 5 kinds of scenes.
datasets.hand: Custom pressure gloves + Rokoko mocap gloves

sensor.note: 256 raw channels per hand; the release code maps 138 (left) / 147 (right) of them, of which 15 / 24 are finger bend sensors, leaving about 123 pressure taxels per hand. Remapped to a hand-shaped 21 x 21 grid; the glove also streams an IMU quaternion.

scale.text: ~20 h, 1,891 episodes, 208 tasks, 1,000+ objects, ~2.1M frames, 5 scene types

datasets.access: Hugging Face, 88.5 GB.
caveats: The paper reports 256 channels per glove; part of them are bend sensors, so the pressure taxel count (about 123) is derived from the release code.
Release counts differ from the paper: 1,933 episodes / 213 tasks on Hugging Face against 1,891 / 208 in the paper.

tracking.note: 21 joints per hand, transformed into the Vive frame via the wrist tracker when calibrated (rokoko_hands.json).
Three trackers (chest, left_wrist, right_wrist) via OpenXR; 7-D poses in vive_poses.json.
Release also ships wilor_hands.json (1,930 episodes) and hamer_hands.json (1,536 episodes).

other: glove IMU quaternion per hand
finger bend sensors in the glove stream
glove/object segmentation masks (masks.npz, subset)
manual contact annotations
task/object/scene metadata

sources: local: ~/data/ext/egotouch (episode files, split.json; ffprobe of chest/left/right.mp4)
unconfirmed: Camera models not stated. Egocentric camera is called head-mounted in the main text but 'chest/head-mounted' in the appendix; files are chest.mp4 and the Vive role is 'chest'. README calls it a 'wide-angle' camera.

taxels_per_hand=256 is the raw channel count. The released mapping (pressure_position_mapping_*.json) uses 138 (L) / 147 (R) unique channels; configs/hand_joint_positions.json marks 15 (L) / 24 (R) of them as finger bend sensors, leaving ~123 (L) / ~129 (R) pressure channels.
Glove maker not named ('custom pressure-sensing gloves'); raw file is named jq_pressure.json, which suggests but does not establish a JQ Industries glove.
Release counts differ from the paper: HF lists 1,933 episode folders / 213 tasks; local split.json lists 2,228 episodes / 228 tasks; paper and README say 1,891 / 208.
Number of participants not stated.
scenes/scene_types from the paper's five environment categories, confirmed by the release's top-level folders (Home/Office/Outdoor/Retail/Workbench).
taxels per hand (123) derived from the release's channel mapping, not stated in the paper
Glove maker from a figure on the TouchAnything project page labelled 'JQ-Industries Fabric Tactile Glove'; the paper text says custom pressure gloves.

used_by.note: All training and evaluation data, from the Hugging Face release zhouzhoujy/EgoTouch. 1,926 of the 1,933 episodes in the authors' copy (20.21 h) are cut into 43,604 clips of 49 frames; LoRA fine-tuning runs one epoch over 38,600 clips (17.51 h, 1,338 episodes, 174 tasks), and evaluation uses 3,000 clips from held-out recording sessions (2,728 in-distribution, 272 out-of-distribution). used_by.name: Ego2Contact, arXiv 2610.22932
used_by.note: Human training data, with a seen-object test set of 179 episodes and an unseen-object test set of 85 episodes; compared against TouchAnything, which the authors reproduce.

used_by.name: TouchAnything, arXiv 2605.13083
used_by.note: Trained and tested on EgoTouch: 1,891 episodes split 80/10/10 by episode, with the test set divided into seen and unseen objects; 25 epochs on a frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14.

used_by.name: TouchWorld, arXiv 2607.07287
used_by.note: The tactile world model (Wan2.2-TI2V-5B with LoRA) is pretrained on EgoTouch egocentric and wrist video, hand pose and bilateral palm pressure maps, converted to visual-tactile goal grids, then fine-tuned on 10 h of the authors' Wuji-hand robot data. The amount of EgoTouch used is not stated.

datasets.name: T-Rex
datasets.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Bimanual teleoperation on two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands with five fingertip tactile sensors each, in LeRobot format.
datasets.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on Dexmate Vega-1

sensor.note: Five fingertip sensors per hand (Sharpa Wave built-in). Per sensor: raw sensor image (320x240 grayscale), estimated deformation map (240x240 grayscale), estimated 6-axis net wrench. Recorded at 30 Hz with the teleop loop. No palm sensing.

datasets.name: EgoTactile

datasets.name: HRDexDB
datasets.title: HRDexDB: A 4D Dexterous Grasping Dataset Across Human and Multiple Robot Embodiments
datasets.summary: Paired human and teleoperated robot grasps (Allegro V5 Plus, Inspire RH56F1 and RH56DFTP, Robotiq 2F-85 on an xArm6) over 100 objects, filmed by a 23-camera rig with MANO hands and object 6D poses; built-in tactile only on the Allegro and Inspire F1 hands.
datasets.hand: Human hand (no tactile); Allegro Hand V5 Plus (16 DoF), Inspire RH56F1, Inspire RH56DFTP, Robotiq 2F-85, each on an xArm6

sensor.note: Robot hands only. Allegro V5 Plus: raw/hand/tactile.npy (T, 4) int32, one value per fingertip sensor, ~99 Hz, 0 to ~1,800 counts. Inspire RH56F1 (right hand): raw/hand/right_tactile.npy, one dict per sample with normal_force, tangential_force and tangential_direction for 8 regions (little, ring, middle, index, thumb, palm_right, palm_middle, palm_left) = 24 scalars at 50 Hz. Inspire RH56DFTP: tactile.npy is empty in all 618 episodes; a per-actuator force.npy (T, 6) at ~50 Hz is present. Robotiq 2F-85: none. Units are not stated. Paper: readings too noisy or sparse to serve as contact labels.
sensor.model: Allegro Hand V5 Plus fingertip tactile sensors; Inspire RH56F1 built-in tactile; Inspire RH56DFTP finger force sensors

caveats: The release has 1.29 h of play data in 38 recordings, while the paper reports 2.5 h. The 449,188 tactile samples in the release do match the paper's '450k frames'.
The paper says 640x480 RGB cameras, but the released AVIs and depth arrays are 1280x720.

The tactile values are uncalibrated. The paper calls them 'susceptible to hysterisis' and says they 'can change when strong magnets or metals are in the vicinity'. Each recording starts near zero, so the values are offsets from the state at the start of the recording.
Depth files are empty (800-byte HDF5 with no datasets) in play demonstrations 16, 19 and 21 and in book_opening demonstrations 7 and 8 (both cameras).
Play recordings have one camera (cam_0). Task demos have two (cam_0, cam_1).
Depth is 41.6 of the 50.3 GB compressed release. All other files of a recording total 17-487 MB, mostly the MPEG-4 Part 2 AVI.
Pad-to-finger mapping is not documented. The code pads one empty slot before pad 0 and the tactile image gives pads 0-2 their own column, so pads 0-2 are probably the thumb.

Most of a play recording is idle or failed motion. The paper subsamples to frames where the fingertips and end effector moved more than 1 cm (play) or 2 cm (demos), and the released *_indices.pkl files hold those subsampled indices.

episodes=70 counts the 38 play_data/demonstration_* folders and the 32 evaluation/<task>/demonstration_* folders. Per task: joystick 8, cup unstacking 7, bowl unstacking 6, bottle cap 6, book opening 5. The paper says 6 per task.
rate_hz=100 is the paper's figure. The record_frequency attributes in the files read 98.2-99.3 Hz for tactile, 299 Hz for Allegro, 50 Hz for Kinova and 29-30 Hz for the cameras.

principle=magnetic is inferred from two statements: the paper's 'can change when strong magnets or metals are in the vicinity' and XELA's 'Our sensors can have interference from nearby magnetic fields'. Neither source names the transducer.
Coverage tip+phalanx is inferred from '4 on each finger and 3 on the thumb' and the camera images. Palm sensing is not reported.

The tactile axis meaning comes from the paper ('tri-axial force reading (forces in translational x, y, z)'). Which axis is normal is not documented. In the data, z is mostly positive under load (max ~2,000), while x and y take both signs.

Camera model: the paper says only 'Realsense'. Depth is uint16 z16 aligned to color according to Holo-Dex realsense_camera.py, which T-Dex uses for recording. The depth unit is not stated (the RealSense default is 1 mm); the median non-zero depth in joystick demo 6 is ~400-500.
Camera role 'third_person, static' is inferred from the frames: play cam_0 and task cam_0/cam_1 view the hand and table from fixed positions.

Units of Allegro/Kinova positions (rad), Kinova Cartesian position (m) and fingertip position (m) are inferred from magnitudes. Kinova joint angles reach ~7.1, so they are unwrapped. Effort units and the quaternion order are not stated.
scene_types 'lab tabletop' is inferred from the camera frames. The number of scenes, play objects and teleoperators is not stated.
The tracking method vision_estimate for Holo-Dex follows from the paper's 'The headset returns a pose estimate for each finger' and the Fig. 2 'Oculus Headset'. The headset model is not named.

datasets.summary: Teleoperated Unitree G1 and H1 humanoids on 246 everyday tasks; the G1 episodes carry Unitree Dex3-1 hand pressure sensors (9 per hand).
datasets.hand: Unitree Dex3-1 (7 DoF) x 2 on G1; Inspire (6 DoF) x 2 on H1

sensor.note: G1 episodes only: observation.tactile.values (18, 4) float32 + sensor_id 1-18, NaN-padded to 4. The release's observation.tactile.values (18, 4) is shifted by 13 values: the recording code (GitHub teleop/master.py + worker.py, commit 9611546) writes 13 odometry values and then 216 pressure values (left 9 x 12, then right 9 x 12) but reads the pressure block from where the odometry starts, reshapes to 18 x 12 and keeps indices [0, 2, 9, 11] or [3, 6, 8] per row. Release row k, kept index i is true value p = 12(k-1) + i - 13 (hand p // 108, sensor (p % 108) // 12, element p % 12; p < 0 = odometry), so a release row is not a sensor. After undoing the shift only 22 of the 66 Dex3-1 readings survive (12 left, 10 right); the right hand's palm 2 and 3 fall off the end, the other kept values are 30000 (no reading) or odometry (release row 1 and row 2 col 0). H1/Inspire episodes have empty tactile arrays.

scale.text: Paper: 10.3k trajectories, 260 tasks in 7 categories, 3M+ frames @30 Hz. HF release: 8,949 episodes, 246 tasks, 3,436,171 frames (~31.8 h); tactile G1 part: 4,064 episodes, 124 tasks, ~16.5 h

datasets.access: Hugging Face USC-PSI-Lab/humanoid-everyday, ungated, LeRobot v2.1, one parquet per episode (~935 GB, depth and LiDAR inside the parquet); tactile only in the G1 episodes of this full release, not in the lite G1/H1 repos.
caveats: Tactile only on G1 / Dex3-1 episodes (4,064); H1 / Inspire episodes have empty tactile arrays.

observation.tactile.values is shifted by 13 values relative to the Dex3-1 pressure array (recording-code bug): release row 1 and the first value of row 2 hold odometry, every other kept value belongs to a different sensor than its sensor_id, and only 22 of 66 readings survive (12 left, 10 right; right palm 2-3 lost). The viewer undoes the shift.

Units are not documented, and Unitree's sensor-to-finger map could not be read (the order used comes from third-party G1 code); values sit near 101 kPa and rise by at most a few hundred units during manipulation.
The lite repos Humanoid-Everyday-G1/-H1 carry only joints, actions and video: no tactile, depth, LiDAR, IMU or odometry.
meta/episodes.jsonl 'instruction' is the same string for all 8,949 episodes; use meta/tasks.jsonl via task_index.
License differs between sources: HF card says Apache-2.0, GitHub README says MIT.
Release (8,949 episodes, 246 tasks) is smaller than the paper's 10.3k / 260; 5 episodes were dropped for zero valid frames.

tracking.system: Dex3-1 (G1, 14 hand joints) / Inspire (H1, 12 hand joints) joint states
Unitree G1 (29 DoF) / H1 (27 DoF): 14 arm + 15/13 leg-waist joints, IMU, odometry

tracking.note: teleoperation: finger keypoints from the headset's cameras -> dex-retargeting to the robot hands
teleoperation: wrist poses -> Pinocchio IK for the arms; head/wrist poses are in the raw data.json schema, not in the HF LeRobot release

other: Livox LiDAR point cloud (~3.4k-5.2k points/frame in the release)
IMU
odometry

https://huggingface.co/datasets/USC-PSI-Lab/humanoid-everyday data/*/episode_*.parquet tactile columns of 20 random G1 episodes
unconfirmed: hours=31.8 derived from the HF release: 3,436,171 frames / 30 fps. G1 part: 1,779,287 frames (16.5 h), H1 part: 1,656,884 frames (15.3 h), from meta/episodes.jsonl lengths.
Tactile task count 124 = distinct task_index over robot_type 'g1' episodes in meta/episodes.jsonl; tasks are split 124 G1 / 122 H1 with no task on both robots.

taxels_per_hand=33, coverage and range are Unitree's Dex3-1 product spec (9 sensors: 2x2 palm x3, 2x2 finger pad x3, 3x1 fingertip x3); the paper only says the Dex3-1 hands 'possess tactile sensors'. Release-to-sensor mapping: the 13-value shift is derived from the release's recording code (teleop/master.py + worker.py at 9611546) and checked on all frames of the 8 sampled episodes: release row 1 and row 2 col 0 equal odometry position x, z and quat w, y, z (max |diff| 0), and every recovered non-30000 value lands on its true sensor's element set (A = 0, 2, 9, 11 on pads and palm, B = 3, 6, 8 on fingertips; 0 violations). Surviving readings per hand (sensor, element): thumb pad 11, thumb tip 8, middle pad 2 and 11, middle tip 8, index pad 2 and 11, index tip 8, palm 1 2 and 11, plus left palm 2 and palm 3 element 11. Sensor order per hand (thumb pad, thumb tip, middle pad, middle tip, index pad, index tip, palm 1-3) is from third-party G1 code (i2ca/prometheus-vla g1_utils.py), not a Unitree document; the data agree (only sensors 2, 4, 6 carry type-B readings). Left-first order is from the recording code and agrees with joints and video in one-handed episodes 3422, 8208, 8174.

Unit not stated; readings near 1.01e5 suggest absolute pressure in Pa (inferred from magnitude). Rises above the episode's 5th percentile were 32-720 units in 10 sampled G1 episodes, and <=50 in episode 0 while the left hand holds a phone stand, so contact visibility is unverified.

22 live release cells (column 0 of rows 3-18, column 2 of rows 3, 5, 7, 12, 14, 16) and the odometry in rows 1-2 were observed in 20 of 20 random G1 episodes, not all 4,064; after the shift these are the 22 readings listed above.
Camera model D435 is from the GitHub README calibration section; the paper says only 'Intel RealSense RGB-D'. Head mount not stated; inferred from the egocentric view.
LiDAR unit not stated; point norms of ~4,000 suggest millimetres. Depth stored as float32 converted from uint16 (he2lerobot.py); depth unit not stated.
Accelerometer magnitude ~9.87 in episode 0 suggests m/s^2; IMU/odometry units not stated. Odometry is all zeros in the H1 episode checked (40).
Number of scenes, objects and operators not stated; paper says 'indoor and outdoor environments'.
Raw per-task zips (with AVP head/wrist poses, tau_ff, sensor_type) are linked from a Google spreadsheet in the README; that sheet was not opened.

datasets.name: ACE-Data-0
datasets.title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
datasets.summary: Two-handed household tasks at a table-scale home workspace (folding socks, wrapping food, packing a backpack, assembling racks) recorded with ACE-Sense-Glove Lite full-palm pressure gloves (256 or 460 raw values per hand at ~80-92 Hz), a 4-fisheye egocentric headset and 5-8 GoPro views; 541 tactile takes (534 distinct, ~20.5 h) are uploaded so far.
datasets.hand: Human hands, both wearing ACE-Sense-Glove Lite tactile gloves

sensor.note: raw/tactile/{left,right}/take-NNNNNN.parquet, one row per glove packet, every column stored as a string. Two packet formats: shard ACE-Data-Tactile-0 (47 takes) has MAT_0..MAT_459 (PACKAGE_SIZE 460) + sync_time_s, SN, TIMESTAMP at ~91 Hz, of which ~100-108 channels stay 0 in every scanned take (~352-360 live); shards 1-10 (494 takes) have pressure_0..pressure_255 + a glove quaternion (w, x, y, z), imu_raw_hex, a 0/1 contact column, sensor_name LH/RH and packet times at ~80 Hz nominal (42-81 Hz effective, gaps up to 1.15 s), with 76 (left) / 44 (right) channels 0 in all 37 scanned files and 93-187 per take. Values are 8-bit counts 0-255 (255 reached in several takes). No channel-to-hand map is released; units are not stated. The paper describes 'hand-shaped pressure grids remapped from raw glove sensors, with calibrated normalization and baseline correction'; the files hold the raw packets.
sensor.maker: ACE Robotics (by product name; the paper names the maker only for the headset)

scale.text: Tactile part uploaded so far: 541 table-scale takes in 11 shards (534 unique, ~20.5 h; 21-875 s per take, median 108 s; ~730 GB), 435 distinct free-text goals. Planned whole release (all parts, card): 150 h+, 17M+ frames, 75,000+ interaction episodes, 200+ task categories, 50+ participants, 2 sites

datasets.access: Hugging Face ACERobotics/ACE-Data-0: the card defines a personal access form for non-commercial academic research (the gate was not enforced on 2026-10-16); glove data is under Table-scale/Tactile/ACE-Data-Tactile-{0..10}, and per-take parquet and mp4 files can be fetched one by one.

gate.note: The dataset card asks for a personal access form for non-commercial academic research; the Hugging Face gate itself was off on 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-18.

datasets.license: ACE-Data-0 Research License Agreement v1.0 (non-commercial academic research only, no redistribution)
caveats: Only the Table-scale/Tactile shards (541 takes) carry glove data. Room-scale (1,131 takes), Table-scale/HOI (290 takes) and Table-scale/Hands (199 takes) have no tactile files.

The tactile takes ship without body mocap, hand pose, object pose, headset pose or audio: each holds egocentric and GoPro video, one IMU stream, camera calibration and a caption. Mocap, hand poses (raw/hand_poses in HOI), object poses and SMPL-X (Room-scale) are only in the parts without gloves.

Two tactile packet formats in one release: shard 0 (47 takes) stores 460 values per hand (~360 live), shards 1-10 (494 takes) store 256 values per hand plus a glove quaternion and a 0/1 contact column. Neither comes with a channel-to-taxel map, units or calibration; the paper's remapped, normalized, baseline-corrected grids are not in the files.

In shards 1-10 the glove packets arrive irregularly: effective rates of 42-81 Hz against ~80 Hz nominal, with gaps up to 1.15 s; one scanned right-glove file (shard 9 take-000000) has corrupt quaternion rows (norms up to ~1e14).
Shard ACE-Data-Tactile-3 lists takes 8 and 10-15 as byte-identical copies (same LFS hashes for tactile, IMU and every video) of takes 0 and 2-7, so 541 listed takes hold 534 distinct recordings.

The card says the repository is gated and that 'Data files are not published yet', but the Hugging Face API reported gated: false and 22.2 TB of files on 2026-10-16, with uploads still running on 2026-10-14. The card's headline figures describe the planned release and 'will be verified in the final release manifest'.
The license forbids redistribution to anyone not granted access individually (section 3.2), so no sample is re-hosted.

83 of the 535 caption files are placeholders (Task: episode-NNNNNN.mp4, no subtasks) and 6 takes have none. Captions were replaced on 2026-09-07 by repository PRs titled 'Claude-generated task/subtask descriptions'; the paper names Gemini-3.1-pro-preview as the captioner.
Egocentric videos are MPEG-4 Part 2 in shards 1-10 and H.264 in shard 0; GoPro videos are H.264. info.json lists no audio track in any video, and no audio files are in the tactile shards.

The glove is synchronized to the headset by matching an IMU motion pattern performed at the start of each take; the glove streams keep their own packet clock (sync_time_s, take-relative s) next to a 30 Hz reference timeline in data/.

other: glove quaternion per packet (shards 1-10)
IMU: one 6-axis stream per take at 200 Hz (raw/imu; device not named, likely the headset since shards without gloves carry it too)
per-take fisheye calibration (xi, K, D, inter-camera transforms) and GoPro intrinsics/extrinsics (aniposelib toml)
LLM-written task goal and timed subtasks per take
capture rig per the paper, not released for tactile takes: 16 OptiTrack PrimeX 22 cameras, a 41-marker body suit, finger keypoints triangulated from the 8 GoPro views

objects, subjects, scenes = null for the tactile part: the paper gives 25+ object instances in 8+ categories at table scale, 50 participants and 2 sites overall; no per-take subject or object label is released in the tactile shards.

Live channel counts are the channels that leave 0 in at least one scanned take: 360 left / 352 right of 460 (shard 0, 3 files), 180 left / 212 right of 256 (shards 1-10, 37 files). The true taxel count is not stated. The 460-raw / 360-live packet matches HumanTouch's glove (460 raw, 360 valid points per hand); neither source names a shared vendor. Whether the 256-value format is a second glove version or a firmware change is not stated.
The 0/1 contact column (shards 1-10) is undocumented; it is 1 in 8-100 % of packets per scanned file.
Glove maker: the paper credits ACE Robotics for the ACE-Ego-Head-V02 Lite headset only; the glove's maker is inferred from its name.
Coverage tip/phalanx/palm from the paper's 'contact pressure maps across the palm and fingers area' and CoP over 'fingertips and palm'; the released files give no layout.
IMU units read as rad/s and m/s^2 from the ranges (acc_z ~ -9.6); not stated.
Third-person count 8 is the paper's figure; per shard info.json lists 5-8 GoPro streams (shard 0: 5).
Chinese company name 大晓机器人 for ACE Robotics comes from press coverage of the release, not from the card, paper or license.

datasets.name: Daimon-Infinity DM-DataDex
datasets.title: TacExoGaze: A Human-Centric Glove Interface for Multi-View Vision-Tactile Data Collection in Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.venue: Dataset release (Hugging Face, ModelScope), 2026-04-15; TacExoGaze preprint forthcoming
datasets.summary: Both hands of human operators in the TacExoGaze exoskeleton (DM-DataDex) with vision-based DM-Tac X sensors on the thumb, index and middle fingertips, released as per-sensor deformation, shear and depth maps alongside exoskeleton finger encoders, wrist, head and eye tracking, stereo headset video and an RGB-D third view over 22 tabletop tasks.
datasets.hand: Human hands wearing the TacExoGaze exoskeleton glove (DM-DataDex), both hands

sensor.note: Three fingertip sensors per hand (thumb, index, middle; 6 per session when both hands are recorded). Per sensor and frame: a deformation map and a shear map (3 planes each) and a depth map (1 plane), uint16, lossless FFV1 in .mov. 802 sessions (2026-01-23 to 03-03): 320x240 maps at 20 fps. 393 sessions tagged newtac/tacV2 (2026-03-19 to 04-03): 384x288 maps at 30 fps plus the raw 640x480 grayscale sensor image (H.264 mp4). Deformation/shear values sit around 30,000 (offset encoding); scale and units are not documented in the card (decoding is left to the Daimon SDK in the gated Daimon-Infinity-Lite repo).
sensor.model: DM-Tac X (label in the card's DM-DataDex figure: 'DM-Tac X 120FPS Vision-based Tactile Sensors')

scale.text: DM-DataDex part: ~45.1 h, 10,015 episodes in 1,195 sessions, 22 tabletop tasks, 3.93M frames at 20 or 30 fps; ~4% of the hours and 6% of the 37.75 TB in the Daimon-Infinity release (card pie chart: 5%), the rest being DM-DataClaw gripper data

datasets.access: Hugging Face daimonrobotics/Daimon-Infinity, folder DataDex_Datasets/ (ungated; 2.28 TB, one LeRobot v3.0 folder per session, single files downloadable); the ModelScope copy requires an application form.
caveats: This entry covers only the DM-DataDex (TacExoGaze exoskeleton) sessions in DataDex_Datasets/. The rest of Daimon-Infinity (DM-DataClaw/ and the folder named TacExo/, robot_type ugripper_left / ugripper_right / dual_ugripper, ~1,091 h and 35.5 TB) is handheld parallel-gripper (DM-DataClaw) data and is excluded; the TacExo/ folder holds gripper data despite its name.

Two recording formats: 802 sessions at 20 fps with 320x240 tactile maps and no raw sensor image; 393 sessions (folder tags newtac, tacV2) at 30 fps with 384x288 maps plus the raw 640x480 sensor image. The card describes only 384x288 maps and says video and state are unified at 30 fps.
Tactile maps are 16-bit FFV1 .mov files (not H.264), 135-250 MB per sensor per session; deformation/shear values are offset-encoded around 30,000 with no documented scale or unit.
Each stream is one concatenated file per session (5-10 episodes); episodes are cut by from/to timestamps in meta/episodes. Sessions are 0.8-7.4 GB (median 1.6 GB).

Not every session has both hands: 110 sessions record tactile on the left hand only (Orient and place blocks on peg, pen to cup, Wiping whiteboard on laptop), 15 on the right hand only, and 7 have 1-2 sensors on one hand. 43 Store Allen keys sessions have no camera streams.

One wrist pose is nearly constant (position range < 2 cm over the session) in 165 (left) and 335 (right) of 1,094 sessions checked. In the pouring sessions the third-view video shows both hands on the cup while the left wrist pose stays within ~2 mm, so wrist tracking is missing in at least some sessions.
Eye pose (gaze) is constant in 184 of 1,094 sessions, 158 of them 30 fps sessions, i.e. gaze is mostly not recorded in the newer format.

observation.state and action share the gripper/robot layout of the card (114-D / 111-D); robot, gripper and IMU dimensions are the placeholder 9930 throughout DataDex, and action equals the recorded state (human demonstration).

Upload incomplete when listed (repo last modified 2026-10-17): 28 sessions (275 episodes, 1.3 h) lack 510 of their declared video files, 8 sessions have none, and 30 lack meta/episodes and meta/stats.json.
No operator, scene or object labels: DataDex sessions have no episodes_metadata.json; the task label (meta/tasks.parquet) is the only annotation. 'Wiping the whiteboard clean' is spelled two ways.
The TacExoGaze preprint named in the card's citation is not published; the arXiv paper linked from the card (2610.20320, TacClaw-Infinity) covers the gripper data only.

Share of the release: DataDex_Datasets/ is 2,281,886,948,206 B of 37,748,239,156,224 B in the three data folders (HF treesize; DM-DataClaw/ 35.09 TB, TacExo/ 0.37 TB) = 6.0% by bytes. By hours, DataDex 45.1 h vs 1,090.7 h of gripper data (563 DM-DataClaw + 7 TacExo session info.json files) = 4.0%. The card's pie chart gives DM-DataDex 5%.

Hours claims conflict: the card says the first 1,000 h are released and 10,000+ h will be open-sourced, and its statistics section is 'based on approximately 1,209 hours'; QbitAI (2026-04-20) writes '其中 10000 小时数据直接开源' [of which 10,000 hours are directly open-sourced]; the TacClaw-Infinity paper and GitHub README give 10,000+ h collected; the files sum to ~1,136 h (all devices).

tasks=22: 23 task strings in meta/tasks.parquet over all sessions, two of which ('Wiping_the_whiteboard_clean', 'Wiping the whiteboard clean') are the same task. Session folder names carry extra tags (pc, laptop, newtac, tacV2, right_hand) whose meaning is not documented.

Sensor model: the card's DM-DataDex figure labels the fingertip sensors 'DM-Tac X 120FPS'. The 20 fps sessions store 320x240 maps, which matches the 320x240 sensing resolution Daimon lists for DM-Tac F, while DM-Tac X is listed at 384x288 (the size in the 30 fps sessions); which sensor the 20 fps sessions used is not stated.

Deformation and shear: 3 planes each (gbrp16le), decoded values centred on 30,000 (e.g. 29,950-30,103 in sampled frames), plane 1 never below 30,000; the TacClaw-Infinity paper calls the DM-Tac X output 'three-axis tactile signals'. Axis order, scale and unit are not documented. Tactile depth: one plane, 0 in a non-contact frame and 0-199 in a v2 frame; unit not stated.
Raw tactile images (30 fps sessions) are declared as (480, 640, 1) but stored as H.264 yuv420p 640x480; a decoded frame shows a grayscale speckle-pattern gel image.
Third-view depth: FFV1 gray16le 640x480 with intrinsics for 1280x720 / 640x480 / 640x360 in info.json; camera model and depth unit not stated.

scene_types=['lab']: from 9 third-view frames (8 tasks, 2026-01-23 to 04-01) all showing the same white table in an office-like room; the card says data were collected 'in real environments' and gives no scene list. Several different operators are visible; their number is not stated.

Wrist-tracker and gaze dropout counts come from the per-session min/max in meta/stats.json (1,094 of 1,165 files had a 114-D state; 71 had a different layout and were skipped); threshold 2 cm for wrist position, 0.02 for eye quaternion components.
action vs observation.state in tacexo_Fold_the_towels_pc_0206_110646: same values at lag 0 (mean absolute difference 1e-5, max 0.03 on eye quaternions).
fps of the egocentric and third-view streams in the 30 fps sessions taken from info.json (fps 30); ffprobe was run on 20 fps session files only (H.264 640x480 at 20 fps).

The 1,062-value vector has no documented taxel order; data.json tactile_names is empty. Pad sizes come from the paper's Table 10.
No per-frame timestamps in data.json; the paper states 30 Hz logging. data.json info declares 640x480 images, but the released JPEGs are 1280x720.
data.json text fields are template placeholders in the checked episode ('task description', 'step1: do this; ...'); only the goal string ('pick up cube.') varies.

Release counts differ from the paper: 29 sub-task folders and 8,174 episodes vs 28 sub-tasks and 8,000+ successful trajectories (Table 8: 8,021 successful of 10,622).
data.pkl is a pickled pandas DataFrame; load only in a trusted environment.

datasets.name: Dex-MPTD
datasets.title: TacCompress: A Benchmark for Multi-Point Tactile Data Compression in Dexterous Hand
datasets.summary: PaXini DexH13 four-finger hand with 11 three-axis tactile arrays (1,140 units) grasping 8 objects in 4 grasp poses, 10 repeats each; tactile signals only.
datasets.hand: PaXini DexH13 (4 fingers, one rotary motor per finger)

sensor.note: 11 arrays on the four fingers: distal and proximal arrays 120 units each, intermediate arrays 60 units each; every unit reports a 3-axis force (normal and tangential) in its local frame. The paper stores 8 bits per axis and converts each recording into a 1,140 x T x 3 image for compression. No palm sensing.

scale.text: 4 grasp poses (pinch, tripod, cylindrical, spherical) x 8 objects x 10 repeats = 320 grasps; recording length per grasp and frame count not stated

datasets.access: Paper: 'Our codes and dataset will be released upon acceptance.' The workshop paper is published (Oct 2025), but no release was found on Hugging Face, GitHub or ModelScope on 2026-10-17.
caveats: Grasp-and-hold only: the hand lifts the object 0.3 m, holds it 15 s and releases it; recording starts 10 s before the grasp.
Tactile only: no camera, joint or pose stream is described as part of the dataset.
Recording rate not stated; 100 Hz appears only in a bandwidth example (100 Hz x 1,140 units x 3 axes x 8 bits).
Units and calibration not stated; raw values are 8 bits per axis.

other: 48 V DC supply and PaXini hand controller (collection platform, Fig. 2)

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2505.16289v2 (Sec. 3.1-3.2, Sec. 5, header with MSMA '25 and DOI 10.1145/3728485.3759170)
unconfirmed: episodes = 320 derived from the stated design (4 poses x 8 objects x 10 repeats); the paper gives no trial count.
tasks = 4 counts the grasp poses; objects: apple, egg, orange, tomato, potato, vitamin bottle, water bottle, glass bottle.
rate_hz left null: 100 Hz is used only to illustrate bandwidth in Fig. 1's caption.
Coverage tip + phalanx from 'distal, intermediate and proximal sensors' on the four fingers; per-finger sensor count (11 over 4 fingers) not broken down.

Sensing principle of the PaXini arrays not stated in the paper. The catalog's hardware entry paxini_dexh13 (which already cites this paper) lists DexH13 GEN2 as magnetic (Hall array, PX-6AX GEN2 units); the generation used for Dex-MPTD is not stated.

datasets.name: DexTacWAM
datasets.title: DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands on a teleoperated Dexmate torso, recorded with ten fingertip gel images, marker-flow fields and 6-axis wrenches per frame over a 488-episode pretraining corpus and six task sets of 96-100 demonstrations.
datasets.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on a Dexmate dual-arm torso (7 arm joints per side); 3 of the 6 task sets use the right hand only

sensor.note: Five fingertip sensors per hand (thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky). LeRobot sets, per sensor and frame: 'tactile' grayscale gel image 192x256 uint8 (the raw sensor image is 240x320), 'tactile_flow' 24x32 grid x (dx, dy, magnitude, divergence) float32, precomputed; task sets also 'deform' 192x256 uint8 deformation map (zero outside contact in the checked episode). The 10 x 6-axis fingertip wrenches are not a separate column: they are actions[0:60]. Raw HDF5 repos: tactile_raw (5, 240, 320), tactile_deform (5, 240, 240) uint8 and tactile_f6 (5, 6) float32 per hand at 30 Hz. No palm or phalanx sensing.

scale.text: 1,083 episodes, 655,562 frames (~6.1 h) @30 fps: 488-episode pretraining corpus (250 instructions, 3.5 h) + 6 task sets of 96-100 demos (595 episodes, 2.6 h); 4 more raw HDF5 repos (300 success + 40 failure episodes) outside the collection

datasets.access: Hugging Face collection JensenYuan/dextacwam: 7 ungated LeRobot v2.1 repos (~509 GB, one parquet per episode with images and tactile arrays inside); 4 raw HDF5 + MP4 repos (~305 GB) sit under the same account but are not in the collection or README.
caveats: The 488-episode pretraining corpus re-releases T-Rex recordings (same lab, rig and 21 of T-Rex's 22 motor-primitive verbs): in 48 of 48 checked episodes the 58-D joint-state range lies inside a T-Rex episode with the same primitive and object (2 identical in length and range; corpus 200 = T-Rex 3479 frame for frame). The authors do not say this; it is the catalog's check.

Fingertip wrenches are stored inside 'actions' (first 60 values: left then right hand, thumb..pinky, 6 values each), unit not stated; frames where a finger read all zeros were filled with the previous value during conversion.
Tactile and camera images are downscaled to 192x256 (raw gel image 240x320, raw cameras 640x360). The 488 corpus has the head camera only and no 'deform' column.
Three task sets (unstack bowl, place with tongs, pick-place cube) are right hand only: tactile (1, 5, 192, 256), state 45, actions 75, no left wrist camera.

State and action layouts differ between the 488 corpus (state 58 = joints; actions 136) and the task sets (state 90 / actions 150 bimanual, 45 / 75 right-only, with 4x4 end-effector poses); see data/utils/layout_contracts/arm_layouts.json in the code.

Converted sets hold successful demonstrations only; the raw repos also hold 40 failure episodes, have no dataset card or license tag, and two of them (pick cherry tomato with tong, pick cube in a bag) have no converted counterpart.
Episodes are single-row-group parquet files of 33 MB to 2.5 GB with PNG frames and uint8 arrays inside (no MP4), so one episode's tactile cannot be fetched without its whole column chunk.
207 of the 250 corpus instructions have 1-2 episodes (max 6); the card says there are too few episodes per task to train a policy from it.

tracking.system: Sharpa Wave hand joint positions (22 per hand) and joint targets
tracking.note: state / actions; raw HDF5 *_hand_joint_positions, *_hand_target_joint_positions

tracking.system: Dexmate arm joint encoders (7 per arm) + 4x4 current and target end-effector poses
tracking.note: poses only in the task sets and raw HDF5; the 488 corpus state is joints only

tracking.system: HTC Vive (left/right_vive_pose 4x4 in the raw HDF5)
tracking.note: teleoperation; finger teleoperation device not stated in DexTacWAM sources (the T-Rex card names Manus gloves on the same rig)

other: 10 fingertip 6-axis wrenches per frame (actions[0:60])
precomputed tactile marker flow (dx, dy, magnitude, divergence) on a 24x32 grid per sensor
language task instructions (250 in the corpus, 1 per task set)
episode_provenance.json: raw episode and frame range for every task-set episode

unconfirmed: hours=6.1, episodes=1,083, frames=655,562 summed from meta/episodes.jsonl of the 7 collection repos: 488 corpus 377,788 frames (3.50 h); bottle cap 96 / 58,064; bowl 100 / 36,712; tongs 100 / 55,691; handover 100 / 34,218; wipe 99 / 66,185; cube place 100 / 26,904 (task sets 595 / 277,774 = 2.57 h). Paper and project page say 'roughly four hours' for the corpus; its card says 3.5 h. The 4 raw repos (wipe 100+13 failure, pick cube right hand 100+5, cherry tomato with tong 50+11, cube in a bag 50+11) are not counted; 2 of them are the sources of converted sets (dataset_identity.json source_data_dir).

tasks=256 = 250 distinct corpus instructions (meta/tasks.jsonl) + 6 evaluation tasks. The corpus instructions use 21 primitive verbs (lift and place, wrap, fold, grasp and lifting, close, press, open, peel, reach, wipe, squeeze, cut, insert, pour, extract, screw, shake, dispense, assemble, twist, disassemble) over 210 distinct object phrases; objects left null because no count is published.

T-Rex overlap: 48 corpus episodes (12 chosen + 36 random, seed 0) had their per-dimension state min/max compared with T-Rex meta/episodes per-episode observation.state min/max (both 58-D, layout [L_arm 7, L_hand 22, R_arm 7, R_hand 22]). Every one lies inside a T-Rex episode whose motor_primitive and object match the corpus instruction (47 inside exactly one, 1 inside five incl. the matching one); episodes 200 (= T-Rex 3479, grasp and lift shoes, 555 frames) and 396 (= T-Rex 513, keyboard, 447 frames) match exactly, the rest are shorter, i.e. trimmed. The corpus metadata backup is dated 2026-05-21, before T-Rex appeared on HF (2026-06-11). Task strings differ (corpus 'verb object' vs T-Rex captions). The six task sets are not in T-Rex (3 checked episodes: no containing T-Rex episode; collected 2026-07-24 to 08-09 per directory names). Frame-level check (2026-10-17): corpus episode 200 observation 'state' equals T-Rex episode 3479 'observation.state' in all 555 frames (max abs difference 0.0).

SharpaDex v1.0 overlap: none found. SharpaDex uses a 65-D state with torso joints and 4 RGB cameras and is collected by Sharpa; DexTacWAM uses 58/90-D states and 3 cameras. Only the task name 'unscrew bottle cap' is shared. No episode-level comparison was made.

Robot: the card says 'Dexmate torso with two Sharpa Wave dexterous hands' and the README 'dexmate the 22-DoF bimanual robot'; the Dexmate model (Vega-1 in T-Rex) is not named. Camera models not stated (T-Rex, same rig: ZED X Mini head, ZED X One S wrists).

Wrench: actions[0:60] equals raw HDF5 left/right_hand_tactile_f6 except in filled dropout frames (wipe_whiteboard ep 0 vs raw episode_0004: 213 of 39,780 cells differ, each a held previous value). Component order (Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My, Mz) assumed from T-Rex's f6 naming; unit not stated, values quantized to 0.01 with |F| peaks of 13-23 in sampled episodes, i.e. plausibly N. Right-hand |F| reaches 21.0 in several bowl episodes (possible clip, not checked).

Tactile image size: 192x256 is 0.8x of the raw 240x320 gel image; the resize itself was not traced in code (vtam_data_scripts is not released). deform 192x256 comes from the raw 240x240 map, so it is stretched or padded (not checked). tactile_flow channel order (dx, dy, magnitude, divergence) is from data/tactile_dataset.py; unit not stated.

Raw cameras: ffprobe of pick_cube_right_hand_raw episode_0001 head_left_rgb and left_wrist MP4s: H.264 High 4:4:4 Predictive (lossless-style, gbrp), 640x360, 30 fps, 298 frames = total_steps. Raw HDF5 timestamp steps median 33.9 ms (command_hz 30).

488 corpus actions (136) layout read from values: [0:60] wrench, [60:76] and [76:92] two 4x4 target poses (last row 0 0 0 1), [92:136] 44 hand joint targets; no arm joint targets. Task-set layout from arm_layouts.json and verified against raw HDF5 (state joints exact, poses and targets < 2e-7).

Teleoperation: paper says demonstrations are 'visuo-tactile teleoperation demonstrations'; the device for the fingers is not stated. Raw HDF5 holds left/right_vive_pose (HTC Vive assumed from the name).

used_by.name: DexTacWAM, arXiv 2609.24976
used_by.note: In the paper's own release, 96-100 teleoperated demonstrations for each of 6 tasks (595 episodes) fine-tune the video world model (stage 2) and train the action expert from scratch (stage 3); the 488-episode stage 1 corpus is in the same release.

datasets.name: DextraVerse
datasets.title: DextraVerse: real-robot task (pick_cube_place_box)
datasets.summary: Two Sharpa Wave hands on a Dexmate Vega robot pick a purple cube into an orange box in 261 real episodes (~19.5 Hz), with a 24x24 deformation map and a 3-axis force in N from each of the 10 fingertip sensors, plus head and wrist RGB.
datasets.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on Dexmate Vega (two 7-DoF arms)

sensor.note: Per hand and frame: {side}_tactile_data_fingers (5, 24, 24) uint8 fingertip deformation map (mostly 0 at rest, up to ~200 in contact) and {side}_tactile_data_fingerforce (5, 3) float32 contact force in N in each fingertip sensor's own frame; channel order thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky (area ids 0-4). Forces are not tared: rest |F| is 0.35-2.05 N per finger (median over episodes). No palm or phalanx sensing.

scale.text: Real robot: 261 episodes, 138,382 frames at ~19.5 Hz (123 min), 1 task (cube into box); the 300 simulated episodes (3 tasks, 135,734 frames) in the same repo are not counted

datasets.access: Hugging Face ntumars/DextraVerse, ungated: the real part is one 43 GB stored (uncompressed) ZIP64 of a zarr v2 replay buffer, so single zarr chunks can be range-read; an earlier HDF5 export with actions is on the gated repo Xiongge0212/dextraverse-rig-grasp-n261 (login, auto-approved).
caveats: One real task on one rig: pick up a purple cube and place it in an orange box. 256 of 261 episodes use one hand (140 left, 116 right), 3 use both hands, 2 never grasp; the idle hand's tactile channels stay at rest.
The arm was teleoperated with a SpaceMouse and the hand closed by a learned grasp policy on the operator's command, so finger motion is not human-teleoperated.

No action stream in the CC BY 4.0 export (measured joints, wrist and head-camera poses only). The gated HDF5 original adds 63-D actions, hand joint commands, grasp phase and fingertip sensor poses; its card states no license.

Fingertip forces are not tared: rest |F| is 0.35-2.05 N per finger (median over episodes) and up to ~6.5 N (95th percentile, left index). Some maps are not blank at rest (64 episodes on the left hand, 18 on the right show a value > 20 in the first 20 frames); in episode 229 the left index reads ~4.8 N and a static pattern throughout.
Sampling is irregular: median 19.5 Hz (per-episode medians 15.9-22.1 Hz); episodes 32, 33 and 42 contain recording stalls of 4.8, 5.9 and 1.2 s.
The same repo holds 300 simulated episodes (handover, pick and place, stack cube; Isaac PhysX contact force and synthetic TacMap images, 224x224 renders). They are not counted here.
The hand-joint slot indices (FAAS slots) are a contributor-derived mapping, not one published by Sharpa or Open-X-Tactile.
No paper, project page or code: the card says these 'remain empty at the contributor's request'.

tracking.system: Sharpa Wave hand joint angles, 22 per hand (rad, 0 = open)
tracking.note: {side}_hand_joints + {side}_hand_joints_idx (FAAS slot per joint)

tracking.system: Dexmate Vega 7-DoF arm joints (rad) and wrist pose [x, y, z, rotation vector] in the robot base frame
tracking.note: {side}_arm_joints, {side}_wrist_pose; camera_ego_pose for the head camera
teleoperation of the arm; the hand is closed by a learned grasp policy on the operator's command

other: head camera pose per frame (6-D, fixed within a session)
language instruction per episode (3 variants naming the hand used)
simulated part in the same repo (Isaac PhysX contact force, synthetic TacMap deformation images), not counted

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ntumars/DextraVerse (DextraVerse/joint_mapping.json, supplementary_joints_note.json, supplementary_tactile_note.json, canonical_mapping_evidence.json, SHA256SUMS.txt, commit history)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/ntumars/DextraVerse/blob/main/DextraVerse/pick_cube_place_box.zarr.zip (ZIP central directory, all 11,740 member names; all non-camera zarr arrays and meta/episode_ends read in full, 52.8 MB; camera chunk 0 of each view decoded)
unconfirmed: hours=2.05 is the card's '123 minutes'; the sum of per-episode timestamp spans is 122.8 min. rate_hz=19.5 is the card's 'about 19.5 Hz' and the median frame step over all episodes (0.0512 s); the gated HDF5 card says 20 Hz recording with a 50 Hz control loop.
objects=1: the grasped object is one purple cube; the orange box is the container. Derived from the task text.
scene_types=['lab'] from one decoded head-camera frame (office/lab room, table, bystander); the card does not describe the scene. Camera models are not stated.

Sensing principle 'optical' and type 'vision' come from Sharpa's description of the Wave fingertip sensor as camera-based (catalog hardware entry sharpa_wave); the DextraVerse card only calls the arrays a 'deformation map' and 'contact force'. The 24x24 map size differs from the 240x240 deformation maps T-Rex releases from the same hand; how DextraVerse's map was produced is not stated.
calibrated=true because the card states the force in newtons; it is the hand's own force output, and no calibration procedure is described.

Authors from the simulation README ('Authors, in contributor-specified order: xiangyu chen, chuhao zhou, jiaxiao shi'); the real-robot README names only the contact xiangyu.chen@ntu.edu.sg. Organisation is the HF org 'MARS Lab' (ntumars) and the card's 'MARS Lab, Nanyang Technological University'.

Episode i is demo_i of rig_grasp_merged_20260908_n261.hdf5 (zarr .zattrs source_demos is demo_0..demo_260 in order; the stall episodes 32, 33, 42 match the gated card's flagged demos). Gated card: recorded 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-06 in ten sessions; demos 212-260 come from session_20260904_150927.

Hand used per episode from data/sub_task_instruction: 140 'with the left hand', 116 'with the right hand', 5 with no hand named (episodes 33, 96, 145, 248, 253). Force rises > 1 N on both hands in 145, 248 and 253; none above 1 N in 96; 33 is a no-grasp episode per the gated card but its right fingertips rise by up to 11 N.
The gated HDF5 stores finger_force_mag (10,) and finger_force_dir_sensor (10, 3); that the zarr's (5, 3) force per hand is their product was not checked.
Peak |F| in the release is 44.9 N (right middle); the Sharpa W01 spec range is 0-30 N per the catalog hardware entry.
Not on the Open-X-Tactile site snapshot of 2026-07-17 (15 datasets); the HF card tags it 'open-x-tactile' and the simulation README says organiser acceptance is pending.

datasets.name: DexUMI
datasets.title: DexUMI: Using Human Hand as the Universal Manipulation Interface for Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Human hand in a 3D-printed exoskeleton matched to the XHand or Inspire robot hand, with the XHand's own magnetic fingertip sensors (thumb, index, middle) or FSRs on the exoskeleton fingertips, joint encoders, an under-wrist OAK-1 W camera and iPhone ARKit wrist pose; only a 544 MB sample is public, with fingertip force in one 15.8 s XHand reference episode.
datasets.hand: Human hand in a DexUMI exoskeleton matched to the ROBOTERA XHand (12 DoF) or the Inspire hand (6 DoF); the released sample is XHand only

sensor.note: XHand exoskeleton: XHand fingertip tactile modules on the thumb, index and middle exoskeleton fingertips, read over UART; the recording code keeps only each module's resultant force (fx int8, fy int8, fz uint8), so numeric_1/2/3 fsr_values are (T, 3) int64 per finger; the 120-point per-module force arrays are parsed out but not stored. Inspire exoskeleton (not in the sample): ZD10-100 force-sensitive resistors through a voltage divider. XHand data recorded at 30 fps (paper; 29.9 Hz measured for index and middle, 23.9 Hz for thumb in the sample).
sensor.maker: ROBOTERA (XHand fingertip tactile modules); generic ZD10-100 FSR (Inspire variant)
sensor.model: XHAND 1 fingertip tactile sensor mounted on the exoskeleton

scale.text: Paper: 310 cube-picking, 175 egg-carton, 400 tea-picking (stated 'for both Inspire Hand and XHand') and 370 + 100 kitchen trajectories over 4 tasks. Public sample: 3 XHand-exoskeleton episodes (13.5 s and 12.2 s without touch, plus a 15.8 s reference episode with touch) and 2 robot replays

datasets.access: Sample zip (544 MB, real.stanford.edu/dexumi/sample_data.zip, linked from the GitHub README) with two XHand-exoskeleton episodes, their XHand replays and one reference episode; the full dataset is not released, and the README's 'All data collected by us' link goes to the UMI dataset list, which has no DexUMI entry. Hardware CAD, firmware and code are on GitHub (MIT).
caveats: Touch is recorded in one 15.8 s reference episode only; the two demonstration episodes in the sample have no tactile streams (numeric_0 joint encoders only) and their replays have none either.
The XHand fingertip modules have 120 sensing points each, but the recorder stores one resultant 3-axis force per fingertip (int8 fx, fy; uint8 fz), 3 fingertips per hand; the unit is not stated.
The sensors sit on the human-worn exoskeleton, not on a robot; robot-side data in the sample are replays (hand motor values and robot-hand video) without touch.
Paper: the XHand sensors drift after high pressure, and the Inspire FSRs are sensitive to how they are attached.
The demonstration data of the paper (~1,355+ trajectories over 4 tasks on two hands) are not public.

Data come as zarr v2 groups (blosc-lz4) and mp4 files inside a single zip; mp4 entries are deflate-compressed with the moov atom at the end, so a video cannot be probed without fetching its whole entry.

datasets.name: EgoExplorer
datasets.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
datasets.summary: Whole-body human loco-manipulation in 5 rooms (6 laboratory procedures, 4 household and industrial tasks), recorded with a head-mounted GoPro HERO13, 5 VIVE Ultimate trackers and gloves; the Wuji glove configuration (41% of regular recordings) adds a 24x31 pressure matrix with 526 active taxels per hand.
datasets.hand: Human hands x 2 in Wuji gloves (tactile + EMF finger tracking) or MANUS Metagloves Pro (EMF finger tracking, no tactile)

sensor.note: Wuji recordings only. Per 30 Hz release row: 2 x 24 x 31 normalized taxel readings with invalid cells masked, plus 2 x 17 binary regional contact with separate validity (thumb 2 regions, other fingers 3 each, palm 3). The 24 x 31 matrix (744 cells, row-major) has 526 active points (maker spec; the paper's health mask also retains 526 of 744). Native rate 120 Hz nominal, resampled to the 30 Hz grid; contact is the logical OR of native detections in each 1/30 s bin. The paper defines raw (L0), baseline-relative (L1) and regional-contact (L2) interfaces and states the values are not calibrated force or pressure.

scale.text: Paper: 2,715 recordings, 100 h, 10 task templates, 5 environments; touch in 41% of regular recordings (Wuji gloves). Released: mini release of 18 recordings, 118,910 frames at 30 Hz (66 min), all 10 tasks

datasets.access: Hugging Face InternRobotics/EgoExplorer, gated behind a Google form that is checked automatically (access in about a minute); it holds the 66-min mini release (18 recordings, 21.1 GB), and the full collection opens in stages through a waitlist.

gate.note: Hugging Face lists the gate as manual approval; the gate asks for a Google form that the project says is checked automatically, with access in about a minute. It covers the 66-min mini release; the full collection opens in stages through a waitlist.

caveats: Only the 66-min mini release (18 recordings) can be downloaded; the paper's 2,715 recordings (100 h) are opened in stages to waitlisted groups.
Touch exists only in Wuji-glove recordings: 41% of regular recordings. The MANUS recordings (58%) have finger articulation and no tactile data.

Released taxel values are normalized readings with invalid cells masked; the paper calls them contact indicators and says they are not calibrated force or pressure. The GitHub README describes them as 'calibrated taxels'.
Tactile is resampled from ~120 Hz native to the 30 Hz grid; regional contact is the logical OR of native detections inside each 1/30 s bin.
Paper statistics mark the right-hand index and central-palm regions n/a: fewer than three recordings have 30% or more live taxels there.

Whole-body SMPL-X is reconstructed from 5 trackers (head, wrists, ankles); 17 joints are inferred. The 18.0 mm / 20.3 mm body-point errors are measured against tracker-fitted reference labels, with no optical mocap reference.
Step annotations are VLM drafts reviewed by operators; the expert audit of drafts found factual errors in 11.09% of segments before correction.

The card and paper name the video key observation.images.ego; the mini release stores it as observation.images.camera_0. The repository also holds a per-task zarr copy (dataset/oxt/EgoExplorer/<task>.zarr) that the card does not describe.
Number of participants and objects not stated.
The release files were not opened for this survey (gated, access not requested); channels come from the card, the paper and the file tree.

tracking.system: Wuji glove or MANUS Metagloves Pro: five 6-DoF fingertip EMF sensors per glove, 120 Hz nominal

other: step annotations (step ID, free-text description, interval bounds, skill, object roles, observed outcome)
per-episode refined SMPL-X parameters (episode_meta/<episode>/smplx/smplx_episode.npz)
per-episode calibration profile and quality report
validity masks, source-time mapping and interpolation flags per stream

https://forms.gle/2tT2dTxAYXgGXBkK6 (access form and its terms of use)
unconfirmed: Mini release counts (18 episodes, 118,910 frames, 66 min) are the card's; the files are gated and were not opened. The tree has 18 episode_meta folders (episode_000001-000018), 18 data shards and 18 camera_0 MP4s.

One episode per shard is inferred: data/chunk-000/file-i.parquet, videos/.../file-i.mp4 and episode_meta/episode_(i+1)/smplx_episode.npz sizes rise and fall together (video/data ratio 35-62). The card says a shard may hold several episodes.

In the card, the mini release keeps 17-region contact under episode_meta/<episode>/, while the paper's Table 9 puts it in every row; episode_meta holds annotations/, calibration/, metadata.json, quality/ and smplx/ only, so it is not clear which file carries contact.

Hand representation: paper Table 9 gives 2 x 45 SMPL-X finger rotations per row; the card's mini-release list says both hands' 21-joint skeletons; the paper's fitting keeps 20 non-wrist landmarks from a 25-node glove layout.

The zarr copy (dataset/oxt/EgoExplorer/, one group per task, ~13.7 GB) has arrays camera_ego_rgb, camera_ego_pose, left/right_wrist_pose, left/right_hand_pose, left/right_hand_joints(_idx), left/right_tactile_{data,sensor,type,area}_wuji each with _contact and _score variants, sub_task_instruction, timestamps and meta/episode_ends. Shapes, rates and meanings were not read (gated) and are not documented.
120 Hz is the manufacturer's nominal glove rate (paper Table 8); per-recording timing follows native timestamps.

Taxel count: the Wuji product page states '24 x 31 Pressure Sensor Matrix (526 active points)'; the paper says its health mask, estimated from earlier recordings, retains 526 of 744 taxels. Sensing principle not stated by either.
Coverage 'phalanx' comes from the paper's 17-region map (3 regions on each non-thumb finger); the maker page states only full palm coverage.

Project page says '100+ hours' growing by 5 h/day and that the dataset, toolkit and reconstruction code 'will be released'; the GitHub README dates the toolkit code to early November 2026 (repository holds only README and assets on 2026-10-16).
The paper reports 545 regular Wuji recordings with healthy tactile on both hands and 565 recordings with 1,110 healthy hand streams; the total number of Wuji recordings is not stated.
Laboratory tasks are 41% of recordings (46% of duration); the other environments: study 23%, industrial workspace 17%, food-preparation area 11%, living room 8%.

datasets.name: EgoTac-SC
datasets.title: EgoTac: In-the-wild Tactile Prediction from Egocentric Vision
datasets.summary: Bimanual in-house motion-tactile gloves (60 finger + 72 palm force channels per hand, 11 nine-axis IMUs) with HTC VIVE wrist trackers and a head-mounted ZED 2i, in 857 clips (~36 h, 3.9M frames at 30 Hz) of 70+ household tasks in 24 environments; released with 224x224 egocentric RGB, glove forces, hand and wrist poses and MANO-mapped force and contact.
datasets.hand: AetherGlove motion-tactile gloves on both hands (EgoTac paper: 'in-house'; release folder 'aether_v1')

sensor.note: Per hand: <side>_finger_tactile (T, 5, 12) + <side>_palm_tactile (T, 72) float64, force per channel (paper: calibrated force in N, contact threshold 0.05 N); 0.0-4.4 in the clips checked, 77-78% of values exactly 0. Raw streams were resampled to the 30 Hz camera timeline by linear interpolation. Five bend-related channels per glove and the IMU signals are not released. Also mano_tactile_<side> (T, 778) float32 force mapped onto MANO vertices and mano_contact_<side> (T, 778) uint8 (mapped force > 0.05 N).
sensor.maker: Aether Embodied Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. (named in FTP-1's acknowledgments); the EgoTac paper calls the glove in-house
sensor.model: AetherGlove (motion-tactile glove; 'aether' / 'ether' in the release names)

scale.text: 857 clips, 3,896,609 frames @30 Hz (~36.1 h), 70+ tasks (e.g. folding clothes, wiping tables, opening doors) in 24 environments; clips 5-632 s (median 137 s), recorded 2025-11-20 to 2025-12-30

datasets.access: Hugging Face wkzhang/EgoTac-SC, ungated: 857 Zarr clips (458 GB) packed whole into 45 stored ZIP shards of ~10 GB with a manifest.json that maps clips to shards; linked from the project page and code README. A second repo, wkzhang/EgoTac-SC-OXT (created 2026-10-12), holds only a README.
caveats: Egocentric video is released only as 224x224 resized and cropped frames; the 1080p ZED 2i video, depth and point clouds, and the raw HDF5/SVO recordings are not released.
No task, environment or participant label per clip: each Zarr holds only data arrays and meta/episode_ends; clip names are millisecond timestamps.

Tactile units are not stated in the release; the paper evaluates EgoTac-SC force in newtons (error < 0.06 N, contact threshold 0.05 N). Bend channels and the 11 IMUs per glove are not released; hand pose is a processed 20-joint 6-D array.
MANO force and contact fields are interpolated from the 132 glove channels through predefined patches, not measured per vertex.
Glove-recoloured RGB and glove masks exist only in shards 1-16; shards 17-45 carry the plain RGB only.
Every clip sits inside a ~10 GB stored ZIP; one clip needs HTTP range reads of the central directory (Zip64) and its entries, or the whole shard.
Participants wear black gloves, so the RGB shows gloved hands (the paper discusses this visual-domain gap).

<side>_wrist_pose (T, 6)
head pose; source device not stated

calibrated=true and unit N rest on the paper (calibrated force prediction on EgoTac-SC, force MAE in N, contact = mapped force > 0.05 N); the dataset card and processing docs do not state units. Values are floats, 0 at rest on 77-78% of entries, peaks 0.4-4.4 in 9 clips checked.

tasks=70 is the paper's 'more than 70'; scenes=24 is the paper's '24 diverse environments'. Neither is labelled per clip. The clips span 24 recording days (2025-11-20 to 2025-12-30, from the millisecond clip names); frames checked show bedrooms, a kitchen, a living room and a dining table, hence scene_type 'home' in addition to the paper's 'kitchens, offices'.
Paper wording differs: '264 force sensors' (2 x 132) in Sec. 3.3, 'more than 120 sensing points' per glove in App. B. The release has 132 per hand.
coverage 'tip': each finger has one 12-channel block; where on the finger it sits is not stated.

head_tracker_pose source is not stated (the paper lists VIVE trackers only for the wrists).

Modules sit on thumb + index tips in 45 trials and middle + little tips in the 7 trials of 2026-08-05/06. The hardware also reports per-taxel forces; they are not released.

sensor.note: One row per video frame. Kitchen force_{left,right}_aligned.csv: sensor0-5 (filtered, baseline-subtracted, normalized; 0 to ~2.5), force (combined contact signal), force_row_idx (-1 = no glove sample); Kitchen/P13 also has raw_sensor0-5 + raw_force. Lab force_aligned_.csv (right hand): sensor0-4 processed + raw_sensor0-4 (ADC counts, 0-565 in P1) + raw_force + force. Masked drift or malfunction intervals are NaN. Sensor-to-finger order not documented.

scale.text: Paper: ~27 h, ~3M force-synchronized frames of kitchen manipulation. Release: 13 Kitchen + 21 Lab participant recordings (622 GB); readable force CSVs index 1.81M frames (Kitchen 1.07M without P05, Lab 0.73M; Lab P20, P21 have no CSV)

datasets.access: Hugging Face edessa/feel, ungated, 622 GB: one uncompressed rgb.tar of JPEG frames per participant (0.5-54 GB) plus per-frame force CSVs (0.4-15 MB).
caveats: The release holds video frames and glove force only. Audio, eye gaze, MPS hand tracking, contact labels and contacted-object masks described in the paper are not in it.
Force columns are processed values without units; the README says the preprocessing targets contact detection and that force magnitudes need a different pipeline.
Kitchen/P05 force CSVs are not text: binary content whose sha256 matches the stored LFS object. Lab/P20 and Lab/P21 have frames but no force CSV.

Lab recordings (848x480 frames from a camera behind the participant, right glove, 5 sensor columns) are not described in the paper; the camera is not named. The first Lab/P1 frame shows laptop typing at a desk.
No task labels or episode segmentation: one continuous recording per participant, 3-64 min at 30 fps.
Masked intervals are NaN; the README says to treat them as missing, not zero. Lab/P1 sensor0 and sensor4 are NaN for the whole file.
No timestamps file; frame rate not stated.
The README points to Kitchen/participant_mapping.tsv; the file is not in the repository.
Lab/P21 holds 4,707 JPEGs that OpenCV cannot decode (README).

other: recorded, not released: Aria audio (7 mics), SLAM cameras, IMUs, eye tracking, MPS hand tracking and 6-DoF trajectory

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/edessa/feel (README.md, preprocess.py, .gitattributes, full repo tree via API)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/edessa/feel force CSVs: Kitchen/P06, P09, P12, P13 (both hands), Lab/P1 (+ before_reprocess), P6, P11, P19; head and tail range reads of every CSV; first 2 MB of Kitchen/P12 and Lab/P1 rgb.tar
unconfirmed: Frame rate not stated. 30 fps is derived from the paper (~3M frames / ~27 h = 30.9 fps) and fits the project-page clip times (Lab/P9 has 19,123 frames and a clip ending at 598.5 s, so its rate is at most 32 fps).

Release frame counts are last frame_idx + 1 of each CSV (range reads): Kitchen 1,072,092 over P01-P04, P06-P13; Lab 733,434 over P1-P19. Estimated from rgb.tar bytes per frame: Kitchen/P05 ~88,600, Lab/P20 ~35,800, Lab/P21 ~9,600. Total ~1.94M frames (~18 h at 30 fps), below the paper's ~3M frames / ~27 h; scale.hours and scale.frames are the paper's figures.
sensors_per_hand=6 from the paper (one per fingertip + a palm strip). Lab CSVs carry 5 sensor columns; whether the Lab glove lacks a sensor is not stated.
The arXiv HTML renders the sensor count as '55' and the range as '4545 N' (duplicated digits from math markup); Sec. 3.1 and Fig. 4 give six sensors per glove and 45 N (~10 lbs).
subjects not stated: 13 Kitchen and 21 Lab folders use separate anonymized IDs; overlap between them is not stated. README calls Kitchen/P12 'the Yianni recording' (author Yianni Karabatis).
scenes=2 counts the release's top-level folders (Kitchen, Lab); the number of kitchens is not stated.

Kitchen frames are 1408x1408 fisheye JPEGs (Aria Gen 1 RGB native); the paper says 1440x1440. Lab frames are 848x480; the first Lab/P1 frame shows the participant's head from behind, so the Lab camera is not head-worn. README mentions unuploaded depth/ directories.
Venue from the project page ('ECCV 2026 (oral presentation)'); arXiv v1 lists none.

Column meaning from the paper (Hampel filter, smoothing, rolling-percentile baseline, normalization by the 99.5th percentile, geometric mean of sensors = combined signal) and preprocess.py (raw_sensorN = original readings; force_aligned_.before_reprocess.csv = backup before participant-specific ignore rules).
Kitchen/P05 force CSVs: 2,767,495 and 2,072,576 bytes with ~8 bits/byte entropy, no gzip/zlib/xz header; sha256 of the left file equals its LFS oid fc6edb82..., so the upload itself is unreadable.

Real-world object pose is a pseudo-ground-truth from three-camera tracking with scanned meshes (paper); where it is stored in the release was not confirmed.
data.pkl is a dill pickle and was not opened; the official loader reads time, allegro.base_pose, allegro.joint_state, digit_info and realsense.<camera>.intrinsics/pose from it.
