datasets.name: Sharpa North-FTP-1
datasets.title: FTP-1: A Generalist Foundation Tactile Policy Across Tactile Sensors for Contact-Rich Manipulation
datasets.summary: Bimanual demonstrations on Sharpa North robots with two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands, released in FTP-1's zarr format with 224x224 fingertip deformation maps for the thumb, index and middle finger of each hand, a head and two wrist RGB cameras and joint states at ~30 Hz.
datasets.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on Sharpa North

sensor.note: <side>_tactile_data_fingers (T, 3, 224, 224) uint8 per hand: one single-channel deformation map per fingertip for FTP-1 functional areas 0, 1, 2 (thumb, index, middle tip); ring and little fingertips are not in the release. Maps are dark at rest with a bright contact blob. Rest level differs between sessions (24 in tube_season_POC22007_2026_02_09, 0 in fixSharpaHandModel_V2_season_POC22007_2026_03_08); contact peaks of ~200-230 were seen. No raw sensor image and no force/wrench values are released in this subset.
sensor.model: Sharpa Wave fingertip tactile sensor (paper: 'Sharpa DTC'; product page: Dynamic Tactile Array)

scale.text: Open-X-Tactile listing: 9,328 trajectories, 7,902,778 frames (~73 h at 30 Hz), 12 tasks; paper: ~4,000 long-horizon demonstrations; 1.86 TB of zarr stores recorded on two robots (POC22007, POC22018) between 2026-01-15 and 2026-03-21

datasets.access: Hugging Face MJJJJ1064/FTP-1-Dataset (ungated) or ModelScope Eureka1064/FTP-1-Dataset, folder sharpa/: one 1.86 TB tar split into 20 parts holding one zarr store per recording session; there is no per-episode file, so an episode is fetched by indexing tar headers with range reads.
caveats: The ModelScope mirror's metadata gives 'MIT License'; the Hugging Face card, paper, project page and Open-X-Tactile page state no license. At least three of the 12 tasks share recording sessions with SharpaDex v1.0, which Sharpa releases under CC BY-NC 4.0.

Recordings overlap with SharpaDex v1.0: 15 of 92 sampled sessions have the same robot and session timestamp as SharpaDex seasons (pick_place_pen = place_pens_in_holder, charger_into_the_socket = insert_plug_into_socket, Tidy_up_the_books = place_books_on_shelf). In session POC22007_2026_03_16_15_28_42 FTP-1 has 52 episodes and SharpaDex 37, and all 37 SharpaDex episode lengths appear in the same order in FTP-1. Sessions before 2026-03-10 (tube, gear, usb_charger, power_strip, drawOnBalloon, most SciExperiment_V2 and fixSharpaHandModel_V2) are not in SharpaDex.

Only 3 of the 5 Wave fingertip sensors per hand are released (thumb, index, middle), as 224x224 deformation maps; SharpaDex releases raw and deformation videos plus 6-axis values for all 10 fingertips of the shared sessions.
Processed for FTP-1 pretraining: images resized to 224x224, no commanded action array (FTP-1 derives targets from future states), language from GPT-4o rewrites (paper).
Units are not stated for any stream; joint values look like radians, poses like metres + rotation vectors (FTP-1 docs: (x, y, z, rx, ry, rz), z forward, x right, y down).
The middle-fingertip map of the right hand stayed at its rest value in all 29 chunks sampled from tube_season_POC22007_2026_02_09; whether that channel is dead in some sessions is not checked.
Counts disagree: the paper says ~4,000 demonstrations, Open-X-Tactile lists 9,328 trajectories and 12 tasks; 10 task names (11 spellings) were seen in 92 sampled sessions.
Sessions hold 50-100 episodes each (two checked); the tar must be range-read member by member, ~30,000 members per session.

Other FTP-1-Dataset archives are not covered here. MotionTrans (Franka arm + 6-DoF Inspire right hand) has no tactile sensor: its only touch-related signal is the hand's 6 actuator force readings (right_tactile_data_fingertorque (T, 4, 1) + thumbtorque (T, 1, 2), raw values about -31 to 860), which FTP-1 maps to finger-joint torque slots 16-20. The other 13 archives are grippers or UMI rigs (FreeTacMan, RDP, RDP_Bimanual, RH20TCfg5Franka, RH20TCfg6ATIAxia, RH20TCfg7Tactile, Unit, Unit_Bimanual, VLA_touch, ViTaMIn, VisuoTactile_D-WHEEL, VisuoTactile_QINGLOONG, exUMI). The card announces 18 archives and lists 15; the paper's glove and hand sources (EgoTac, OpenTouch, OmniSharingDB, OpenLETDex, HumanoidEveryday, DexUMI) are not in the release.

tracking.system: Sharpa Wave 22 hand joints per side
tracking.note: <side>_hand_joints (T, 22) + FAAS slot ids; <side>_hand_pose (T, 33, 6) and <side>_hand_keypoints (T, 33, 3) per hand

tracking.system: Sharpa North 7-DoF arm joints + wrist pose
tracking.note: <side>_wrist_pose (T, 6) xyz + rotation vector; camera_ego_pose (T, 6); torso/other 'motor_joints' (T, 7)

other: per-frame language instruction (sub_task_instruction)
head camera pose
33-point hand link poses and keypoints per hand

sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13102 (abstract page and HTML: Sec. 2.4, App. C Table 7, App. E Table 8, acknowledgements)

sharpa/sharpa.tar.part-0000 and part-0001: HTTP range reads of every array header (31 data arrays + meta/episode_ends) and the small arrays of tube_season_POC22007_2026_02_09_15_57_16_train.zarr, 30 right-hand tactile chunks, and episode_ends of pick_place_pen_season_POC22007_2026_03_16_15_28_42_train.zarr; 200 sampled 0.5 MB windows across all 20 parts for session names
MotionTrans/MotionTrans.tar: first 2 MB (one zarr's tactile arrays)
unconfirmed: hours=73.2 derived: Open-X-Tactile frame count 7,902,778 / 30 Hz. Measured time step in one session: median 0.0337 s (29.7 Hz) from data/timestamps (unix s). The paper states no rate for this subset.
episodes=9,328, frames and tasks=12 are the Open-X-Tactile listing, not counted from the files; the paper says ~4,000 demonstrations. Not reconciled.

Task names seen in 92 sessions sampled from 200 evenly spaced windows: SciExperiment_V2 (24 sessions), usb_charger (12), fixSharpaHandModel_V2 (12), tube (8), gear (8), pick_place_pen (7), Tidy_up_the_books (6), power_strip (5), charger_into_the_socket (4), drawOnBalloon_V2 (4; one 'drawOnBalloon_v2'); one store is named 'power_strip_ .zarr'. Robots POC22018 (51) and POC22007 (40); dates 2026-01-15 to 2026-03-21.

Overlap with SharpaDex v1.0 found by session ID: 15 sampled FTP-1 sessions (POC22007 2026-03-16 to 03-20, POC22018 2026-03-17) are SharpaDex seasons; SharpaDex's earliest season is 2026-03-10. Episode-level match checked for one session only (52 FTP-1 vs 37 SharpaDex episodes, all 37 lengths matching in order).

Functional areas 0, 1, 2 read as thumb, index and middle fingertip from FTP-1's area figure (definition_tactile_torque_function_area.png). The maps look like the deformation images that T-Rex releases for the same sensor (dark background, bright contact region); FTP-1 does not say whether they are deformation or processed raw images.

Principle optical: inferred from the T-Rex release of the same Sharpa Wave sensor (raw camera images of an elastomer); neither FTP-1 nor Sharpa's product page names the principle. Range 0-30 N and 240x240 are the Wave W01 product spec, not stated for this data.

Sharpa North: the paper names the robot 'Sharpa North' (Table 8) and its figure shows an upper-body humanoid with head and two arms; Sharpa's site uses 'North' in a customer story and sells the D01 robot with Wave hands and 7-DoF arms. Whether North and D01 are the same robot is not stated.
Teleoperation method is not stated in FTP-1; SharpaDex (sharing some sessions) describes human teleoperation.
motor_joints (T, 7) matches the first 7 columns of supplementary_joints (T, 9, last two 0); its meaning (torso or waist) is not documented. neck_joints (T, 2) has no stored chunks (fill value 0).
Camera model and mounting are not stated; 'camera_ego_rgb' is taken as the robot head camera from the hardware figure.

datasets.title: FusionX Multimodal Sample Dataset (V2 and V3)
datasets.summary: Two TouchTronix conductive-fabric tactile gloves (5 x 4x3 finger patches + 4x15 palm per hand, raw 0-255, glove ~197 Hz resampled to 30 Hz, one bend sensor per finger) with an OAK-D Pro W egocentric camera (720p RGB, 640x400 mono stereo, depth in V2), in 37 short recordings (~20.5 min) of first-aid kit, strap, water pouring, box cutting, drilling, screwing and syringe tasks.
datasets.hand: TouchTronix FusionX conductive-fabric tactile gloves, both hands

sensor.note: Per hand and camera frame: <hand>_<finger>_pressure (12,) uint8 for thumb, index, middle, ring, little (4x3 each) + <hand>_palm_pressure (60,) uint8 (4x15), raw 0-255; *_pressure_cal = raw minus the per-taxel zero in calib.json (not a physical unit); finger_bend (5,) raw + finger_bend_cal 0-1 normalised; glove IMU quaternion. Glove sampled at ~197 Hz (dataset_info: glove_measured_fps; 'fps': 188) and matched to each 30 fps camera frame by nearest neighbour.
sensor.model: FusionX conductive-fabric tactile glove (data format of the v1-conductive-fabric SDK)

scale.text: 37 recordings, ~20.5 min, 36,991 frames @30 fps: V3 repo 11 recordings (first-aid kit x3, strap x4, water x4; 8.8 min, 2026-05-07), V2 repo 26 recordings (box cut, drill, screw/unscrew, syringe, water pour x5 each + 1 test; 11.8 min, 2026-03-13)

datasets.access: Two ungated Hugging Face repos, touchtronix/FusionX-Multimodal-Sample-Data-V3 (15.9 GB, per-frame JPG/PNG folders) and -V2 (19.8 GB, H.264 RGB + lossless depth MKV + zipped frames); one folder per recording with frames.parquet holding all glove data.
caveats: The repo labels V2 and V3 are dataset versions, not glove generations: both use the conductive-fabric glove format (4x3 per finger, 4x15 palm, one bend value per finger). The catalog's FusionX V3 thin-film glove (5 x 4x4, no palm) is a different sensor and is not in these files.
Tactile values are raw 0-255 counts; the '_cal' columns are zero-offset subtracted (calib.json tactile_zero_*), not force or pressure units.
Finger tracking is one bend value per finger (raw and min-max normalised), not joint angles; no wrist position.

Glove gyro and accelerometer are all zero in the V3 recordings (only the quaternion is populated); the V3 OAK IMU sits in a separate oak_imu.parquet on the device clock (~199 Hz), while the V2 frames.parquet carries it per frame.
Glove samples are matched to camera frames (nearest neighbour, 30 fps); the full ~197 Hz glove stream is not released, and glove_timestamp equals the frame timestamp (glove_dt_ms 0).
Task names exist only as folder names (firstaid1, strap2, waterpour3, ...); no task descriptions, objects or subject counts are given.
Short sample release: 37 recordings of 15-96 s; V3 has no depth stream.
Separate from the provider-supplied FusionX clips in the catalog viewer (source 'fusionx', thin-film glove).

The channel-to-sensor map is not released; UniTacHand (same authors) splits the 137 channels into thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky, palm and 'bend' regions. The paper projects the glove onto 891 MANO UV vertices and a 351-taxel UniTacHand space for training; the release carries the raw 137-D vectors.

scale.text: Paper: 37.2 h, 947 episodes, ~4M frames at 30 Hz (the DeskTask-Tac part of the 160 h H-Tac). Released: 14-episode sample (10 RawHand, 4 AprilTag), 22,078 frames (~12.3 min), 12 task names

datasets.access: Hugging Face BeingBeyond/H-Tac_Sample, ungated: 14 DeskTask-Tac episodes (LeRobot v2.1-style parquet + one head-camera MP4 each); the GitHub README says the full H-Tac release is 'coming soon' (checked 2026-10-16).
caveats: Only the DeskTask-Tac part of H-Tac (37.2 h of 160 h) is catalogued. HOI-Tac (~106 h, 124.8K sequences) derives binary contact from hand-object mesh distance in 14 public datasets (ARCTIC, DexYCB, OakInk, ...), and InternData-Tac (17.8 h, 9,563 episodes) projects simulated robot-gripper contact patches (Genie1, Lift2, Split ALOHA) onto a MANO hand; neither is measured touch on a hand, so both are excluded.
Released data is a 14-episode, ~12.3 min sample of the 947 announced episodes; the same repo also holds 84 InternData-Tac episodes (351-D simulated tactile), which are not human touch.
The Hugging Face card has no license tag; the MIT terms are in the LICENSE file of the sample package ('Copyright (c) 2026 H-Tac dataset authors'). The code repository is Apache-2.0.

Tactile values are raw integer counts (0-180 in the sample) with no stated unit; many channels read above zero at rest, and 0-73 of the 137 channels per hand stay at zero for a whole episode. AprilTagPip episode_000001 (operate_calculator): 73 right-glove channels read zero throughout and the right hand shows no contact.
state.dexhand_position, action.dexhand_position and the MANO beta (shape) vectors are all zeros in the 14 sample episodes.
AprilTag episodes: wrist pose and MANO theta are exactly zero in frames where a hand was not tracked (6-177 frames per hand per episode).
Only one camera view is released (video.top_view, the head-mounted first-person RealSense view despite its name); the two external D435 views and depth are not in the sample.
The project URL printed in the paper (beingbeyond.github.io/TTP/) returned 404 on 2026-10-16; the page is at research.beingbeyond.com/ttp.

datasets.title: HumanTouch: A Multimodal System for Scalable Human-Hand Tactile Acquisition
datasets.summary: Two-handed tabletop manipulation (10 tasks) recorded with Moxian piezoresistive gloves (360 mapped taxels per hand) worn under MANUS MetaGloves, with HTC VIVE wrist and head poses, one head camera and two wrist cameras, all resampled to 60 Hz.

sensor.note: observation.tactile.raw_left / raw_right: (460,) float64 per hand = a 23 x 20 grid. meta/humantouch/tactile_mapping.json assigns 360 cells (palm 15 x 16 = 240, 6 x 4 = 24 per finger) and leaves 100 unassigned. Raw values 0-247 in 24 checked episodes, integer ADC counts except where interpolated onto the 60 Hz timeline. Also observation.tactile.patch_pressure (12,) = (left, right) x (palm, thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky), a processed per-region value that is 0 at rest; the episode metadata labels it newton, the project page says these outputs are relative and uncalibrated.
sensor.model: Fabric Tactile Data-Acquisition Glove (matched by layout; HumanTouch names only 'Moxian Gloves')

scale.text: Release: 17,608 episodes, ~132.8 h at 60 Hz (28.7M frames), 10 tabletop tasks; project page: ~100 h, 13,469 episodes (10.0 h per task); 1,000 h announced

caveats: Touch values are uncalibrated: the project page says the outputs "are not calibrated pressure, force, or object-load measurements", while each episode's data_contract says pressure_unit "newton" and the page's comparison table ticks "Force Calibration".

The release is larger than the project page describes: meta/info.json lists 17,608 episodes / 28,674,858 frames (~132.8 h); the page's Fig. 8 shows 13,469 episodes and 10.0 h per task (~100 h). Per task the release holds 10.8-17.7 h.

The Hugging Face copy is incomplete: X008 has 711 of 744 parquets (episodes 194-225 and 228 missing; all 744 are on ModelScope). X005 has a parquet, episode JSON, head and left-wrist video for episode 361, which episodes.jsonl and info.json do not list and which has no right-wrist video.
One tactile_mapping.json serves all tasks. In 3 of 24 checked episodes the 15 x 4 strip beside the palm, marked unassigned, reads up to 87, so the 360-cell mapping may not fit every glove.
Task names, subtask labels and captions are in Chinese only; English task names appear only in the project page's Fig. 8.
All streams are resampled onto one 60 Hz timeline (linear interpolation for tactile and positions, SLERP for rotations); the glove's native rate is not stated.
Episode metadata has no operator, glove or site ID.
Videos are HEVC (head 1920x1080, wrists 1280x960, 60 fps) and make up 1.98 of the 2.09 TB.
A 1,000 h release was announced for the end of September 2026; on 2026-10-16 both mirrors hold the 10-task release (HF last modified 2026-09-06).

datasets.summary: JQ (juqiao) fabric tactile glove, 132 raw ADC taxels per hand (12 per fingertip, 72 on the palm), recorded with one static RGB camera and reconstructed MANO-based hand states over 11 pick and manipulation recordings of household objects, two of them bimanual.
datasets.hand: JQ tactile glove (right hand; both hands in 2 of 11 recordings)

sensor.note: Per recorded hand: <side>_tactile_data_fingers (T, 5, 12) and <side>_tactile_data_palm (T, 1, 72), raw 8-bit ADC 0-255 stored as float32. All 12 finger taxels sit on the distal link of each finger; the palm block has 56 taxels on the palm and 16 on the thumb base link (channel_mapping.json). Each 10 Hz value is the median of the raw samples within +/-50 ms of the camera frame (raw glove rate about 81 Hz, 4,745-5,759 samples per recording); no baseline subtraction, threshold or force calibration. 132 of the glove's 256 raw channels are bound; left and right mappings differ.

scale.text: 11 recordings (45-90 s), 16 continuous spans, 7,126 frames at 10 Hz (11.9 min), 10 household objects; 8 single-object picks, 1 single-hand manipulation, 2 bimanual

datasets.access: Hugging Face lilfiiiiish/juqiao-glove-0929, ungated, 3.3 GB of Zarr v2 directories (one per recording, one blosc-compressed RGB chunk per frame).
caveats: Very small: 11 recordings from one day (2026-09-29), one external camera, 10 objects; 9 of 11 recordings have the right hand only, and an absent hand has no arrays (no zero filling).

Tactile values are raw ADC with standing readings: in the first 5 frames of every recording most regions already sum to 6-140 ADC, and the pinky and palm regions are almost never 0, so contact has to be judged against a baseline. The README warns of glove and posture noise and says a low ADC does not certify no contact.

Hand state is a 21-D vector of FTP-1 geometric angle features in radians plus a 6-D wrist pose (metres, rotation vector) in the camera frame, reconstructed by an unnamed method; the README says it is not motion-capture ground truth. Depth, extra RGB views and IMU from the capture were not released.
Instructions were drafted from file names ('Pick up the cola can.') and are flagged as needing review; the 16 spans are data-continuity breaks, and 4 recordings start with a 1-frame span.
Published 2026-10-16 as an Open-X-Tactile (OXT) contribution; OXT acceptance is not claimed. pinkcup_pick_0929 was excluded (missing visual timestamps).

ScienceDB's file-preview endpoint returned one restricted glove file as an .xlsx without approval during this survey; it was deleted unopened and nothing in this survey is based on it.

datasets.summary: Automated grasp-and-lift trials with a 16-DoF Tilburg Hand on an xArm7 carrying four Digit 360 fingertips (tactile images, stereo audio, IMU, pressure), filmed by a side RealSense D435i; 10,000 trials over 200 objects with manual stability labels.
datasets.hand: Tilburg Hand (16 DoF, 4 fingers, right) on xArm7

sensor.note: One Digit 360 per fingertip (thumb, index, middle, ring). Per sensor: 690x690 JPEG tactile frames (30 Hz nominal, ~24.6 Hz in the checked trial), stereo 48 kHz WAV, pressure + temperature rows (Pa and degC by range, 5-15 rows/s), pressure_ap rows of 2 x 25 uint16 stored as hex strings (26-65 rows/s), raw IMU acc/gyro/mag/aux + quaternion (~11 Hz; absent for thumb and index in the checked trial). All streams carry host perf_time stamps on one clock.

scale.text: 10,000 grasp-and-lift trials of ~12 s (~33 h) over 200 objects (14-123 trials each, median 42); 4,712 stable by manual label

datasets.access: OPARA (TU Dresden), DOI 10.25532/OPARA-1588, no login: 20 zip archives of 10 objects each (40-81 GB, 1.08 TB in total) plus toolkit.zip and object images; the server honours HTTP range requests, so single trials can be fetched from inside a zip.
caveats: The release is 1.08 TB (OPARA size 1,078,004,133,457 B; README: about 1.2 TB), one HDF5 file of 100-137 MB per trial.

Recorded rates are below the nominal 30 Hz: in apple/20260415_112100 the tactile cameras run at ~24.6 Hz, the RealSense at ~26.7 Hz, Tilburg joint states at 25 Hz and Digit 360 pressure at 5-15 rows/s.
In the checked trial the thumb and index Digit 360 have no IMU files (pressure and pressure_ap only); the ring sensor has one dropout row (pressure 0, temperature 787).
pressure_ap channel_a and channel_b are hex strings (100 characters = 25 little-endian uint16 values per row); their meaning is not documented.

Units are not written in most tables: Digit 360 pressure reads ~84,000-108,000 (Pa by range), xArm F/T fx..mz read a few units (N, Nm by range), Tilburg and xArm joints are in degrees by column name and range.
Each trial carries a manual (ground-truth) and an automatic stability label; they agree on 92.34% of trials. Hand closing is open loop: touch does not change the commanded trajectory.
One task (grasp, lift 100 mm, hold 3 s) in one tabletop workspace; the hand never manipulates the object beyond the lift.

caveats: No robot arm or body ('UMI-Dex 无本体数据采集系统' [UMI-Dex robot-body-free data collection system]): a person carries the hand, and the wrist pose comes from a VIVE Ultimate Tracker, not from robot joints.

How the fingers are moved is not stated on the card; finger channels are 6 raw encoder readings (0-255, 'not radians or percent'). The UMI-Dex GitHub hardware folder describes an 'L6 6-DOF serial encoder glove' with finger and arm straps.
Touch is sparse: in 6 segments checked, only thumb and index pads registered; a nail-pinch segment showed no taxel above 0 and an apple segment peaked at 3 counts (sampled every ~0.5 s).
Taxel values are low (peaks of 14-22 of 255 on single taxels in the checked segments); per-finger force reached 0.98-1.2 N.

touch_matrix finger order is 'STM32_FINGER_ORDER' in the message definition; the card states thumb-to-little only for finger_force_mn. In the checked segments the matrix finger with contact matched the force channel with contact.
Right hand only; one operator count not stated.
Wrist images are raw YUYV 640x480 inside the MCAP (~150-390 MB per 8-21 s segment).

Action, sub-action, grasp-type, hand and object labels are generated from the contact signal plus captions (card: 'no human ground truth'); 463 task strings mix action labels with motion captions such as 'The right hand moves away from ...'.

unconfirmed: tasks=5 is the catalog's grouping of the episodes by their dominant action label: container handling (episodes 0-14), whiteboard erasing (15-27, 38-47), box tape cutting (28-37), plant spraying (48-62), sauce pouring (63-71). The release itself has no episode-level task field; meta/tasks.parquet lists 463 strings and annotation.l0_action has 214 distinct values.
rate_hz=90: the card says '90 Hz pressure'; extra/raw_tactile episode 0 has 13,212 (left) / 12,863 (right) rows over 145.7 s = 90.7 / 88.3 Hz. NVIDIA's IsaacCapture OGLO plugin page says 100 Hz.
Raw value range: 0-3,884 seen in the 30 Hz columns over all episodes; 12-bit (0-4095) per the IsaacCapture plugin page. Values are 0 at rest.

Camera models come from meta/opengraph/camera_intrinsics (device.model 'iPhone14,4' = Apple iPhone 13 mini, 'iPhone15,2' = iPhone 14 Pro, lens 'ultrawide', calibration_method 'fov_estimate', 107 / 106 deg horizontal FOV). The card calls it 'a head camera'; the mount is not described further.

Head IMU is inferred to be the phone's: it carries a gravity vector and accelerations of ~0.01 (g scale) at ~100 Hz, unlike the gloves' raw int16 counts. Wrist IMU scale +-8 g / +-2000 dps is from the IsaacCapture page, not the dataset card.
Recording dates 2026-06-25 and 2026-06-26 from the gcs_prefix paths in episode_manifest.json.
scene_types=['tabletop'] from the card ('tabletop manipulation'); one spraying episode is labelled 'hold a blue spray bottle while walking around plants'.
Same layout (5 x 4x4 per hand, 12-bit, wrist IMU) as the TouchTronix FusionX V3 glove; whether the two gloves share hardware is not stated anywhere.

datasets.name: PalmDex
datasets.title: PalmDex: An Embodiment-Agnostic Tactile Manipulation Dataset
datasets.summary: Two 256-channel pressure gloves (raw 8-bit-range readings at 30 Hz) with UDexReal finger tracking and two 640x480 RealSense views (ego and side), over 2,849 episodes (~16.7 h) of lab-bench, electronics and kitchen tasks cut into 12,399 labelled action segments.
datasets.hand: Human hands in 256-channel tactile gloves plus UDexReal hand-tracking gloves, both hands

sensor.note: observation.tactile_left / tactile_right (256,) float32 per hand, 'raw pressure values', no channel names or layout. Values 0-142 in 25 sampled episodes; many channels sit at 20-30 at rest. Only 147 of the 256 channels per hand ever read above 0 in those episodes. Released at the 30 fps video rate; the glove packet counter advances ~198 per second (native rate, from sync_diagnostics).

scale.text: Release (2026-06): 30 sub-datasets, 2,849 raw episodes, 1,804,667 frames @30 fps (~16.7 h), 12,399 annotated segments, 18 task descriptions, 42 action labels, 20 object-set labels, 6 environment labels; the card's summary table still lists the first release (4 sub-datasets, 1,001 segments, 2 tasks, ~8.6 GB)

datasets.access: Hugging Face Rimbot/PalmDex, ungated, 74 GB in 30 per-session folders, each a LeRobot v3.0 raw copy (one parquet and two AV1 mp4 per episode) plus an annotated package of per-segment clips, parquet and labels; anonymous downloads hit the HF rate limit quickly, a logged-in token avoids it.
caveats: Tactile glove maker, model and channel layout are not stated; the tactile values are raw readings with no unit, and only 147 of the 256 channels per hand ever read above 0 in 25 sampled episodes.

The dataset card's summary (1,001 segments, mortar-and-pestle and crucible-tongs tasks, ~8.6 GB) describes the 2026-05-23 first release; the repository now holds 30 sub-datasets, 12,399 segment folders and 74 GB.
Annotated segment clips are MPEG-4 Part 2 (mpeg4), not H.264 as the card states; raw episode videos are AV1.
0508_4_crucible_tongs_transfer ships only the raw LeRobot copy (no annotated folder), and 0515_pharmaceutical_reagent_handling has per-segment meta.json labels but no annotations.jsonl.
Several sub-datasets have sparse episode indices after cleanup (e.g. 0509_5 removed 26 episodes and kept the gaps); the per-folder README lists the removed ranges.
Annotation notes and some grasp_type values are in Chinese (e.g. 双指旋转 [two-finger rotation], 单指推动 [one-finger push]); 87% of segments are labelled 'Small Diameter'.
Environment labels are per sub-dataset; the side view checked for a 'chemistry lab' session (0508_3 episode 4) shows an office desk with a cup, cube and cylinder.

The UDexReal head-bone fields (location, rotation, scale) are 0 in the episode checked; there is no wrist or head pose. The gloves carry printed fiducial markers that the cleanup notes refer to as QR codes, but no marker-based pose is released.
Number of operators and the collection sites are not stated; one sub-dataset is tagged source collection 'changxiang' and the others 'rimbot' or untagged.

tracking.note: observation.udexreal (72,): head bone location/parent/rotation/scale (10, zero in the episode checked) + per hand calibration status, 24 joint parameters, joystick X/Y and 4 buttons; joint parameter units not stated (values roughly -40 to 40). Sensing principle of the UDexReal glove not stated in the release.

other: per-frame sync diagnostics (camera hardware timestamps, tactile sample age, packet counters, stale flags, raw UDexReal JSON)
action-segment labels (environment, object, action, grasp type, success frame, notes)
SHA-256 checksums per package

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Rimbot/PalmDex (README.md, full file listing via the tree API, commit history)
https://huggingface.co/datasets/Rimbot/PalmDex raw data parquets of 25 episodes in 7 sub-datasets (0508_3, 0509_5, 0510_6, 0515, 0507_1, 0509_3, 0509_1)
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jianyi2004/TouchAnything/main/configs/pressure_position_mapping_left.json and _right.json (EgoTouch JQ glove channel maps, for comparison)
unconfirmed: hours=16.7 and frames=1,804,667: sum of total_frames over the 30 raw meta/info.json files at 30 fps; episodes=2,849 is the sum of their total_episodes (0508_4 includes unannotated beaker-stirring episodes). Annotated segments: 12,399 segment folders in the tree (11,483 lines in 28 annotations.jsonl files plus 916 segment folders in 0515), ~11.3 h of segment time in the 28 jsonl files.

tasks=18: distinct 'task' strings in the 30 dataset_metadata.json files (several sub-datasets mix two tasks by episode range, e.g. 0509_5 vacuum-pen chip placement and screwdriver terminal wiring). The raw LeRobot tasks.parquet files only say 'pick and place', 'wash test tube', 'chenmistry experiment' or 'electronic'.

Glove maker: not stated. The set of channels that ever read above 0 in 25 sampled episodes equals the 147 channels of the right-glove map in EgoTouch's JQ Industries glove code exactly, and covers 137 of the 138 left-glove channels plus 10 more (128-137). This suggests the same 16x16-channel JQ glove family as EgoTouch, but the release does not name it. coverage (tip, phalanx, palm) is taken from that match, not from a PalmDex document.

The card says 'UDexReal hand-tracking gloves with integrated tactile sensing', while tactile_routing.txt reads the two tactile gloves from separate serial ports (/dev/tactile_left, /dev/tactile_right) with their own packet protocol (4-byte header, sequence, type 0x01 left / 0x02 right).
Native tactile rate ~198 Hz: tactile_left_count rises from 38,362 to 40,352 over 303 frames (10.07 s) in 0508_3 episode 1 sync_diagnostics.

Camera models: the card says 'Dual RealSense cameras'; models and mounts are not stated. The ego frame checked looks down on the table from above the operator; the side view is static and shows the operator.
subjects not stated; at least one operator is visible in the side view of 0508_3 episode 4.

Episode file layout: in every raw folder checked, data/ and video file-XXX index equals the episode index (one file per episode), confirmed by meta/episodes for 0508_3 episode 1 and by the episode_index inside 24 data files.

datasets.name: PX OmniSharing DB (sample data)
datasets.title: PX OmniSharing DB
datasets.venue: Hugging Face dataset (public sample of a commercial database)
datasets.summary: Bimanual PaXini exoskeleton data gloves with 15 multi-axis tactile sensors per hand (3,465 values per hand), recorded at about 30 Hz with 29 glove joint angles per hand, 11 RGB and 3 RGB-D static cameras and spoken Chinese instructions, over 1,000 episodes of 10 tabletop tasks.
datasets.hand: PaXini exoskeleton data glove x 2 (exoskeleton_hand_left/right_2_0, 29 joints per hand)

sensor.note: observation/<hand>/tactile/data (n, 3465) float32 per hand, split into 15 sensors by the sensor_names / sensor_lengths attributes: palm_sensor1 219, J32L 219, J42L 282, M6L 378, S22L 195, S32L 105, S6L 318, Z22L 195, Z32L 105, Z6L 318, W22L 195, W32L 105, W6L 318, X22L 195, X6L 318. Every length is a multiple of 3, consistent with 3-axis force per point (1,155 points per hand; not stated). Values are signed with 0.1 steps (-1.3 to 25.5 in the checked files); units not stated. An unused hand reads exactly 0.

scale.text: Sample: 1,000 HDF5 episodes (1.08 TB), 10 tasks of 33-200 episodes, 4.5-42 s per checked episode (about 4.8 h estimated from file sizes); the full OmniSharing DB is sold separately

datasets.access: The sample (1,000 HDF5 files, 0.29-4.1 GB each, 1.08 TB) is public on Hugging Face without login; the full OmniSharing DB is sold through the PaXini data mall (dataset-mall.paxini.com).

gate.note: The 1,000-episode sample is public; the full OmniSharing DB is sold through the PaXini data mall.

caveats: The Hugging Face repo is a sample; raw data (DF-1) and the full database are commercial. The card's task table lists 9 tasks with 100 episodes each, while the files hold 10 task codes; the ice-scooping and flower-in-vase tasks found in the files are not in the table, and its 'Insert and Remove' task was not identified.

Tactile sensor layout, axis order and units are not documented beyond sensor names and lengths; the 15 names read as palm plus thumb (M), index (S), middle (Z), ring (W) and little (X) segments, which is our reading.

36Kr (2026-04-21) describes the PaXini PXCap V glove as having 30 six-axis tactile modules and 3,015 tactile points. The sample has 15 sensors per hand (30 per pair) and 3,465 values per hand (6,930 per pair, or 1,155 three-axis points per hand); neither count matches 3,015, and the sample's glove is labelled exoskeleton_hand_2_0, so it may be a different glove version.

Files are large because RGBD_0 aligned depth is stored as an uncompressed (n, 720, 1280) uint16 array (about 1.8 MB per frame); RGB streams are stored as 1-D byte payloads (HEVC for RGB_Camera*, Matroska for RGBD color) and must be decoded.
Task metadata (dataset/meta attributes) and spoken-instruction transcripts are Chinese only. Object pose groups (obj1, obj2) described in the card were absent from all 12 checked files.
Recorded 2025-10-11 to 2025-12-11 according to the generated_time attribute of the checked files.

tracking.note: observation/<hand>/joints (n, 29) with URDF joint names J1J-J4J, M1J-M5J, X1J-X5J, S1J-S5J, Z1J-Z5J, W1J-W5J; 36Kr says the glove uses in-house magnetic encoders
observation/<hand>/handpose (n, 7) [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz]; the card says the sample 'has undergone pose estimation'

other: audio (8 kHz) with Chinese instruction transcript
camera intrinsics, distortion and extrinsics per camera (calibrated 2025-11-17 in the checked file)
stereo left/right images of each RGB-D camera
per-episode task attributes in Chinese (objects, start positions, grasp location, hands used)

sources: data/part_04/episode_1552_220118_108_110095_glove.hdf5 (HDF5 structure and all non-image arrays by range reads)
one HDF5 per task code (11 files in part_01 to part_08): meta attributes, audio transcript, tactile arrays, timestamps, camera list, by range reads (~160 MB in total)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14028 (AdvDex, read 2026-10-27: describes OmniShare, a human demonstration set recorded with a 29-encoder glove and a Hall-effect tactile array)
unconfirmed: AdvDex (arXiv 2608.14028, one author at Paxini Tech, robot experiments on a Paxini Tora with DexH13 hands) describes OmniShare: over 10k hours of video, over 100k trajectories (168k in its Table 1), more than 500 tasks, 721 objects, 14 views, recorded with a glove of '29 magnetic rotary encoders' and a 'Hall-effect tactile array for measuring normal contact forces'. The 29 joints and 14 views (11 RGB + 3 RGB-D here) match this sample, but the paper never names OmniSharing DB and states no release; that OmniShare is the full OmniSharing DB is our reading.
episodes=1,000 counted from the HF file list (100 per folder part_01 to part_10). The recursive tree API returns only 987 of them (pagination); sizes are from that listing.

tasks=10: the fourth file-name field takes 11 values, 9 of them on exactly 100 files and two (108: 55, 91: 45) that both hold flower-in-vase episodes. Task text read from one file per value: 75 disassemble a three-tier file basket; 76 put blocks into a block box (right hand only); 79 clean glasses in an ultrasonic cleaner and wipe them; 81 scoop ice into a cup; 93 brush dust off a keyboard; 91/108 put a flower into a vase; 114 screw a nut onto a hex bolt; 115 put a beer into a rack; 131 connect ribbon cables; 138 assemble a three-tier file basket.
hours not stated. About 4.8 h estimated: the 12 checked files store 2.1 MB per frame (dominated by the uncompressed depth array), and 1.078 TB / 2.1 MB = about 513,000 frames at 30 Hz.
rate 30 Hz from aligned_timestamp steps (33-34 ms) in the checked files; RGB camera timestamps have the same step and different counts per camera (135-181 frames for 136 aligned frames).

sensor.type and principle 'magnetic' from 36Kr: PXCap is built on PaXini's '6D 霍尔阵列式触觉传感技术' [6-D Hall-array tactile sensing]; the release itself does not name the principle. Whether the sample glove is PXCap V is not stated.
coverage tip/phalanx/palm from the sensor names and 36Kr's '全五指无盲区触觉覆盖' [touch coverage of all five fingers without blind spots].
scene_types from the card's task table (Office, Restaurant, Automotive, Home, Industrial, Supermarket, Primitive Action scenes); the checked videos were not viewed.
Subjects not stated; the fifth file-name field (e.g. 110026, 120105) has 10 values whose meaning is not documented.
Not in the catalog's hardware list: the closest PaXini glove entry, paxini_pxcap_pro, lists 1,743 tactile signals and 17 DoF, which does not match this sample.

zh.note: Card and dataset name are English (PX OmniSharing DB); task attributes and spoken instructions inside each HDF5 are Chinese only. 36Kr calls the product 全模态具身智能数据集产品 OmniSharing DB [omni-modal embodied-AI dataset product].

datasets.name: PiMForce
datasets.title: Posture-Informed Muscular Force Learning for Robust Hand Pressure Estimation
datasets.summary: 21 right-handed participants wore a PPS TactileGlove (65 nodes) with 5 Marveldex RA18DIY fingertip sensors, a MANUS Quantum Metaglove and an 8-channel Delsys sEMG armband while repeating 22 press, pinch and grasp postures for 30 s each, 3 sessions per person.
datasets.hand: PPS TactileGlove (65 nodes) + 5 Marveldex RA18DIY fingertip FSRs, with a MANUS Quantum Mocap Metaglove (right hand)

sensor.note: pps_<i>.csv: Time + Elem0-Elem64 (65 TactileGlove nodes), ~1,200 unique timestamps per 30 s (~40 Hz) with each row repeated ~3x; floats with small negative values at rest and peaks of ~1.6 (index press) to ~600 (grasps); unit not stated. fsr_<i>.csv: Timestamp + FSR_1-FSR_5 integer counts at ~99 Hz, 0 to ~600 (FSR_1..5 = little, ring, middle, index, thumb by activity). The paper reduces these to 9 regions (5 fingertips + 4 palm regions) in processing_ours.py.

scale.text: 1,386 trials (21 participants x 3 sessions x 22 postures, 30 s each) = 11.6 h; 7 plane presses, 5 pinches, 10 grasp types

datasets.access: Dropbox shared folder linked as 'Code & Data' on the project page, no login: Dataset_NeurIPS2024.zip (8.2 GB) or the 4,158 trial CSVs (40.0 GB) one by one.
caveats: No video in the release; the paper uses RGB only at inference time.
Trial files are numbered 0-21 per session with no posture labels; the code README says 21 actions. Fingertip activity matches Table 6 except the order of the plane postures (see unconfirmed).

Units: TactileGlove values carry no unit (the code multiplies them by 0.689009, the psi to N/cm^2 factor); fingertip FSR values are raw counts that the code converts to N with Codes/Checkpoints/regression_model.sav.
Pinch and grasp postures hold an object in the left hand while the right hand applies force; the objects are not listed.
The same Dropbox folder holds the code (MIT) and a 63.3 GB Benchmark_PressureVision++_Dataset.egg (5 participants, Logitech Brio webcam + Sensel Morph pad; no glove data).
join_<i>.csv holds 8-channel sEMG at ~1.93 kHz with the MANUS joint angles linearly interpolated onto the same rows (~24 MB per trial).

tracking.note: 120 Hz per paper; 20 joint angles (spread and stretch per finger) in join_<i>.csv, interpolated to the sEMG rows

other: sEMG: Delsys Trigno Avanti, 8 channels in a custom TPU forearm armband

sources: https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/m7qye1l3ii6hlwgzlajyv/ADhaUZvH2eDJ3ggmGAlN5k0?rlkey=eyt5gs66uimhiw3dismnylamw&st=rnrefyzz&dl=0 (recursive listing of all 4,195 files via the share's folder-listing endpoint)
Dropbox Codes/README.md, Codes/LICENSE, Codes/dataset.py, Codes/preprocessing_data.py, Codes/processing_ours.py, Codes/utils.py

Dropbox Dataset/User1/Session1 fsr_0-21.csv, pps_0.csv, pps_14.csv, first 200 KB of join_0.csv; fsr + pps of User4/S2/11, User7/S3/9, User10/S1/12, User13/S2/14, User16/S3/17, User19/S1/18, User21/S2/13
unconfirmed: hours=11.55 derived: 1,980 s per participant (paper) x 21 = 41,580 s; matches 1,386 trials x 30 s in the file tree.
Paper Table 1 lists 83.2M frames, which equals 41,580 s x 2,000 Hz (sEMG samples); frames left null.

File index to posture mapping inferred from fingertip FSR activity in User1/Session1 and 7 other trials: 0-3 single-finger presses (index, middle, ring, little), 4 index+middle, 5 middle+ring, 6-10 thumb+index, thumb+middle, thumb+index+middle, +ring, +little (pinches), 11 no fingertip contact (palm press), 12-21 the 10 grasps in Table 6 order (12 two-finger, 13 thumb only = lateral, 17 all five = medium wrap, 18 four fingers without thumb = fixed hook). Table 6 lists TI-Press and no MR-Press; the PressureVision++ benchmark section lists MR-Press.
FSR_1..FSR_5 finger order inferred from trials 0-3 (FSR_4 index, FSR_3 middle, FSR_2 ring, FSR_1 little) and the lateral grasp (FSR_5 thumb).
sEMG rate: join_0.csv timestamp step 0.518 ms (~1.93 kHz); the paper states 2,000 Hz.

taxels_per_hand=70 = 65 TactileGlove nodes + 5 fingertip FSRs; the paper evaluates 16 of the 65 nodes (4 palm regions) plus the 5 FSRs. coverage lists only what the paper names (fingertips, palm); where the other TactileGlove nodes sit is not documented.
calibrated=null: TactileGlove output is likely psi (factor 0.689009 in the code) but no unit is written in the files or paper.
TactileGlove transduction principle not stated in the paper; RA18DIY are FSRs (paper Fig. 6).
Recording timestamps (e.g. 1707902576 = 2024-02-14) place collection in early 2024.

used_by.name: PiMForce, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv 2410.23629)
used_by.note: 21 participants, 3 sessions each, 22 press, pinch and grasp postures held for 30 s; cross-user tests on participants left out of training.

datasets.name: SynData glove-with-tactile
datasets.title: SynData: A Large-Scale Real-World Multimodal Dataset for Embodied Intelligence (glove-with-tactile subset)
datasets.summary: Bimanual PsiBot exoskeleton data gloves with 256 tactile channels per hand, recorded with a head-mounted RGB-D camera and exoskeleton hand and wrist tracking at 10 fps over 36,780 clips of 34 household and assembly tasks.
datasets.hand: PsiBot exoskeleton data glove x 2 (hand states retargeted to the 30-joint ITW hand model)

sensor.note: left_glove_tactile and right_glove_tactile, (T, 256) float32 per hand, integer-valued counts (0-117 in the checked volumes). Channel layout, sensor type, placement and units are not documented. In two checked volumes at most 156 (right) and 129 (left) of the 256 channels were ever nonzero, and up to 43 channels sat above zero in every frame. Stored on the release's common 10 fps timeline.

scale.text: glove-with-tactile subset: 36,780 clips, 5,236,535 frames at 10 fps (145.5 h), 34 tasks, 310 volumes (2.63 TB)

datasets.access: Hugging Face PsiBotAI/SynData, ungated; the glove-with-tactile subset is 310 .zarr.tar volumes of 0.4-10.9 GB (2.63 TB) plus parquet clip index and annotations. Also mirrored on AtomGit.
caveats: Only the glove-with-tactile subset carries touch. The rest of SynData has none: ego (313,674 clips, 2,765 volumes, 19.8 TB; head RGB, depth and IMU, bare hands), glove-origin (95,383 clips, 793 volumes, 6.55 TB; exoskeleton-glove modalities without tactile) and glove-rep-bg (3,526 clips, 69 volumes, 0.28 TB; background-replaced glove data).
The tactile arrays have no documented layout, sensor type or unit; channel-to-hand-region mapping cannot be recovered from the release.
Hand state is the exoskeleton reading retargeted to an ITW robot-hand model (30 joint angles, 11 keypoints incl. wrist), not human joint angles.
All streams are resampled to 10 fps; head RGB and depth are stored at 640x360 in the checked volume. Depth is float32 millimetres with 0 for invalid pixels.

A clip cannot be downloaded alone: clips are frame ranges inside 0.4-10.9 GB tar archives of Zarr v3 volumes (median 9.0 GB); tar members are 64-frame chunks, so range reads of single chunks are possible.
Press (钛媒体, May 2026) says 1,000 h of SynData are released; the tactile subset is 145.5 h of that.

tracking.note: left/right_qpos (30 joints of the ITW hand model, retargeted) and left/right_fingertip (11 x 3 keypoints)

tracking.system: PsiBot exoskeleton glove system (README: captures both hands and arms with millimetre-level positioning; tracker not named)
tracking.note: left/right_wrist_pose (7,) xyz + quaternion xyzw
head_pose (7,) and head_tracker2head_camera (4 x 4) per frame

other: clip-level task summaries and step-level annotations (scene state, object state, action) in English
head camera intrinsics per frame
ITW hand URDFs and a render script (tools/syndata_render)

sources: glove-with-tactile/tasks/task_0050/000009.zarr.tar (tar headers, zarr.json files and all non-image arrays by range reads)
glove-with-tactile/tasks/task_0026/000023.zarr.tar (tar headers and both tactile arrays by range reads)
manifest.json of ego, glove-origin and glove-rep-bg; HF treesize of each subset
unconfirmed: hours=145.5 derived: sum of num_frames in glove-with-tactile/index/clips.parquet (5,236,535) / 10 fps.

taxels_per_hand=256 is the array width; it is not stated how many are physical taxels. Active-channel counts come from task_0050/000009 (right 83, left 22 ever nonzero) and task_0026/000023 (right 156, left 129).
calibrated=false because values are integer counts with no unit; the README does not describe the tactile signal at all.

Camera mount 'head' from the field names (head_rgb, head_pose); camera model not stated. Resolution 640x360 read from head_rgb/zarr.json of one volume; the README says modalities are not guaranteed to share spatial resolution.
Units of wrist and fingertip positions not stated (ranges -0.8 to 0.8, consistent with metres).
Wrist tracking method not stated; classed 'other'.
Tasks per clip: 34 task keys; clip lengths 0.3-87 s (median 12.4 s).

zh.note: SynData is the publisher's name; the Hugging Face card and README_zh.md write the maker as PsiBot, and Chinese press and the AtomGit mirror write 灵初智能. README_zh.md describes this subset as 带触觉信号的外骨骼手套操作数据集 [exoskeleton-glove manipulation dataset with tactile signals].

datasets.name: PULSE
datasets.title: PULSE: A Synchronized Five-Modality Dataset for Multi-Modal Daily Activity Understanding
datasets.summary: 40 volunteers wore 25-channel fingertip pressure arrays on both hands (values in grams) together with Qualisys mocap, a Myo EMG armband, Dikablis eye tracking and 10 IMUs in 8 household and office scenarios, all resampled to 100 Hz.
datasets.hand: Custom fingertip pressure arrays on both hands (25 channels per hand)

sensor.note: aligned_pressure_100hz.csv: time + R1(g)-R25(g) + L1(g)-L25(g), resampled to 100 Hz from a ~15 Hz native log; channel placement on the fingers not documented. Present in 232 of 337 recordings (69.7% of task recordings). Isolated spikes far above grip level occur (v25/s2 L23 18,688 g, v12/s5 16,433 g).

scale.text: ~9.6 h (S1-S8 6.8 h + S9 2.9 h), 337 recordings (304 task + 33 motion-primitive), 40 volunteers, 8 scenarios, 7,356 action segments over 18 primitives and 54 objects; pressure in 232 recordings (~6.7 h)

datasets.access: Hugging Face velvet-pine-22/PULSE, not gated, 22.0 GB of per-recording 100 Hz CSVs; scene video only for one recording in velvet-pine-22/PULSE-sample.
caveats: Anonymous NeurIPS 2026 E&D submission under double-blind review; authors, institution and the permanent URL are withheld.

The README describes per-recording videos/ folders (scene camera + eye video, ~86 GB in total), but the repository tree has none (22.0 GB); one recording (v1/s1) with both videos is in velvet-pine-22/PULSE-sample.
Pressure covers 69.7% of task recordings: volunteers v1-v22 have intermittent pressure and mocap, v14 has neither.
Pressure is logged at ~15 Hz and resampled to 100 Hz; the layout of the 25 channels per hand is not documented.
LICENSE adds restrictions to CC BY-NC 4.0: no re-identification, no covert worker surveillance or biometric identification, no redistribution of scene video outside academic research.
Action segments were generated by vision-language models and then confirmed or corrected by a human; boundaries have 1 s resolution and cover ~73% of annotated time.
IMU CSV headers are in Chinese (e.g. WT0_加速度X_g [WT0 acceleration X, g]); units are in the header suffixes.
v20/s2 IMU units WT4-WT7 are corrupted; v18/s2 egocentric video froze and has no action labels (README).

tracking.note: 56 joints incl. all 10 fingertips; aligned CSV has 210 columns (Frame, Time, per-marker X/Y/Z/Type); raw Qualisys TSV in raw/
fingertip, finger-segment and hand markers per hand (e.g. Q_RThumbTip, Q_RIndex2, Q_RHandIn)

datasets.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on Sharpa North (two 7-DoF arms + 7 torso/motor joints)

sensor.note: Five fingertip sensors per hand (Sharpa Wave built-in), no palm. Per frame: observation.tactile (60,) float32 = (left, right) x (thumb, index, middle, ring, little) x (fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz), unit not stated; observation.images.tactile_deform, one 480x1200 H.264 video tiling 10 deformation maps of 240x240 (2 rows x 5); observation.images.tactile_raw, one 480x1600 H.264 video tiling 10 raw sensor-camera images of 320x240. Per-episode fz maxima are 5.7-49.8 and torque magnitudes stay below 0.9 in the 23 episodes checked.
sensor.model: Sharpa Wave fingertip tactile sensor (Dynamic Tactile Array)
sensor.range: 0-30 N detection, 50 N maximum load (maker spec, Sharpa Wave W01 page)

scale.text: 28,993 episodes, 59 tasks, 32,396,172 frames @30 fps (~300 h), 495 collection seasons from 11 stations, Mar-Jul 2026; every season is released twice (LeRobot v3.0 and v2.1)

datasets.access: Hugging Face Sharpa-Robotics/SharpaDex-v1.0, ungated, ~7.7 TB (LeRobot v3.0 and v2.1 copies of every season), one LeRobot root per task/season folder; single seasons or v2.1 episode files can be fetched alone.
caveats: Fingertips only (10 sensors); no palm or phalanx touch.
Tactile units are not stated: observation.tactile is called a 'force/torque signal' with fx..tz names. The tile order inside the two tactile videos is not documented.
The card names neither the robot nor the hand ('two 7-DoF arms, two 22-DoF dexterous hands'); robot_type is 'robot' in all 495 seasons.
observation.state.tcp force/torque slots and the 7 torso joint torques are 0 in every episode; TCP units and rotation convention are not documented (rotation_type null).
v3.0 and v2.1 are two exports of the same 28,993 episodes; count them once.
Released as 495 separate LeRobot roots (task/season), not one root; the card recommends splitting by season.
The raw tactile video (480x1600) is the largest stream: ~45-140 MB per 15-50 s episode in the v2.1 export.
Commercial use is prohibited (CC BY-NC 4.0).

Some seasons also appear in FTP-1-Dataset's sharpa/ archive (catalog entry ftp1_sharpa, MIT per ModelScope): 15 of 92 sampled FTP-1 sessions carry the same station and session timestamp as SharpaDex seasons of place_pens_in_holder, insert_plug_into_socket and place_books_on_shelf (POC22007 and POC22018, 2026-03-16 to 03-20). FTP-1 holds more episodes per shared session (52 vs 37 in one checked session) and only 3 fingertip deformation maps per hand. Sharpa's Robotic Origami Challenge and RoCo releases come from the same stations but share no season with SharpaDex.

Hand identified as Sharpa Wave from the maker, 22 joints per hand, and the sensor output matching the Wave W01 spec (240x240 tactile resolution, 6-dimensional force/torque Fx..Mz).

Tactile tiles: 480x1200 = 2 x 5 tiles of 240x240 and 480x1600 = 2 x 5 tiles of 320x240, by division (T-Rex releases the same sensor as separate 240x240 deform and 320x240 raw streams). Principle set to optical from the card's wording ('raw tactile camera layout'); Sharpa's pages call the sensor a Dynamic Tactile Array without naming the principle.

hours=300.0: 32,396,172 frames / 30 fps = 299.96 h; episode and frame totals summed from all 495 v3.0 info.json files (v2.1 episodes.jsonl gives the same); per-task counts match the card's table for all 59 tasks.

Stations: season names carry a station id (POC22002 ... POC22065, 11 ids) and a start time from 2026-03-10 to 2026-07-07; read as collection stations and dates (not documented). Episodes per station: POC22027 7,758, POC22018 6,696, POC22048 6,594, POC22007 2,335, POC22032 1,663, POC22050 1,037, POC22054 994, POC22061 886, POC22065 585, POC22002 423, POC22021 22.
Head cameras are two streams (head_left, head_right); whether they form a calibrated stereo pair is not stated. Camera models not stated.
All 495 v3.0 info.json files list H.264 for the 6 video streams; the card says 'Codec may differ between exports'. Probed: the v3.0 and v2.1 tactile_deform files of one season are H.264 (avc1).
Annotation tags carry 'score' (S or B in the files read) and 'SOP' (V1.0 / V1.1 / empty); their meaning is not documented.
Torso/motor joints (state dims 58-64) are constant in some episodes and move by up to ~0.6 rad in others.
Chinese name: a third-party article (VCA创投社, 2026-09-02) writes 'Sharpa（大裂谷）' [Sharpa (Great Rift Valley)]; no official Sharpa page with a Chinese name was found, so zh is omitted.

The 143 season folders' info.json files list 1,991 episodes; 12 seasons (2026-07-07 to 2026-07-13, 145 episodes) hold metadata only, and v2.1 episode 0 of season 2026-07-09 13:37 has its six videos but no parquet, so 1,845 episodes have data.

The public mirror iris-kaist/origami-v3-merged (and suveen013/origami-v3-merged, same 459 GB) re-packages only the first 46 official seasons (2026-05-14 to 2026-05-30): their v3.0 metadata total 595 episodes and 4,091,138 frames, the mirror's own totals. observation.state.tcp (24 values) is zero in every frame of all 1,991 episodes' stats, and the 7 torso/motor joint torques are zero.

Every one of the 60 channels varies in every episode.

datasets.name: Sparsh-skin dataset
datasets.title: Self-supervised perception for tactile skin covered dexterous hands
datasets.summary: Allegro hand covered with 18 XELA uSkin pads (368 three-axis magnetic taxels on fingertips, phalanges and palm), teleoperated with a Meta Quest 3 through in-hand play with 14 household objects; 140 sequences of ~2 min of raw magnetic signals, XELA force output and hand joint states.
datasets.hand: Allegro Hand (16 DoF) covered with XELA uSkin, on Franka Panda

sensor.note: xela/data.pkl: one (368, 4) float64 array per frame = [t, x, y, z] raw magnetic readings (~32,800 at rest) for 4 curved fingertip pads x 30 + 11 phalanx pads 4x4 + 3 palm pads 4x6; frames at ~93-98 Hz (paper: 80-100 Hz). xela/forces.pkl: (248, 4) [t, fx, fy, fz] per frame from the XELA server, phalanx and palm pads only, unit not stated (|f| up to ~14 in pretraining/ball/0).
sensor.model: uSkin (curved fingertip pads, 4x4 phalanx pads, 4x6 palm pads)

scale.text: Pretraining: 140 sequences of 117-120 s (14 objects x 10), 4.6 h; downstream: 120 relative-pose sequences (~28 s each, one Pringles can) and force-estimation recordings with flat and spherical indenters

datasets.access: Hugging Face facebook/sparsh-skin-dataset, ungated, 54.3 GB of numpy pickles in per-sequence folders; each file downloads on its own (~236 MB per pretraining sequence).
caveats: No license on the dataset card or in the Hugging Face metadata. The code repository (facebookresearch/sparsh-multisensory-touch) is CC BY-NC 4.0; it does not say that this covers the data.

Pretraining sequences hold only allegro/data.pkl (hand joint states) and xela/data.pkl + forces.pkl: no camera, no arm state, no teleoperation stream. The paper says the dataset includes top/left camera views; images exist only for one baseline recording and 2 of the 120 relative-pose sequences.
The paper reports 11 sequences per object; the release has 10 per object (140).
forces.pkl covers 248 of the 368 taxels (none for the four curved fingertip pads); the paper finds XELA's normal-force output inconsistent with F/T ground truth.
Raw magnetic values are uncalibrated and biased; the paper subtracts one baseline recording (pretraining/baseline, hand at rest palm up) and resamples to 100 Hz.

Taxel order and positions are not documented in the sequences; positions come from the hand URDF (pretraining/urdf/ahrcpcpn.urdf) plus forward kinematics. Taxel 145 is zero throughout the checked relative-pose sequence.
Actions are not labelled per sequence; the paper lists squeeze, slide, rotation, pick-and-drop, circumduction, pressing, wiping and articulation.
Allegro joint_states is (T, 33): time, 16 positions (rad by range) and 16 undocumented columns clipped at +-0.5 (likely joint torques).

tracking.note: 200 Hz in the checked sequences

tracking.system: Meta Quest 3 hand tracking + IK retargeting (paper)
tracking.note: teleoperation; headset data not released
relative-pose downstream set only: object_pose.pkl (T, 8) at 20 Hz

other: URDF/xacro of the XELA-covered Allegro hand (taxel geometry)
baseline recording with the hand at rest (XELA, Allegro, RealSense colour)
force-estimation set: F/T-probe indentations of hand pads (flat and spherical indenters)

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/facebook/sparsh-skin-dataset (README.md, API info, full file tree of 6,699 entries)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/facebook/sparsh-skin-dataset files pretraining/ball/0/allegro/data.pkl, pretraining/ball/0/xela/forces.pkl, downstream_tasks/relative_pose_estimation/train/pringle_can/0/{allegro/data.pkl, object_pose.pkl, xela/data.pkl, xela/forces.pkl} (loaded with a numpy-only unpickler)
unconfirmed: hours=4.62 derived from file sizes: each allegro/data.pkl is (T, 33) float64 (264 B per row, checked on 2 files), so T = (size - ~200 B) / 264; at the 200 Hz measured in pretraining/ball/0 the 140 sequences span 117-120 s each, 4.62 h in total. The paper says ~4 h; xela forces.pkl sizes give the same 4.65 h at ~97 Hz.
rate_hz=100 is the paper's resampling rate; raw frames came at 92.9 Hz (relative-pose 0) and 97.6 Hz (ball/0).
The forces.pkl unit is not stated. It is the XELA server's 'forces' field (scripts/xela/convertbag2dataset.py, sensor.forces); values of a few units are consistent with N.
relative-pose sequences ~28 s: 120 sequences, 0.93 h derived from allegro file sizes at 200 Hz; object_pose translations ~0.5-0.6 (m by range).
Force-estimation files (downstream_tasks/force_estimation/*/data.pkl) were not opened; the paper describes an F/T probe applying 0.25-5.0 N.
Hand mounted on a Franka Panda per the paper; no arm stream in the release.

used_by.name: Sparsh-skin, CoRL 2025 (arXiv 2505.11420)
used_by.note: Pretrained on ~4 h of teleoperated play with 14 objects (11 sequences of ~2 min per object; the release has 10 per object, 140); downstream tasks use labelled sets from the same rig.

used_by.name: T-Dex, CoRL 2023 (arXiv 2303.12076)
used_by.note: Third-party: the Sparsh-skin paper (arXiv 2505.11420) reproduces T-Dex's BYOL pretraining as 'BYOL*' on the Sparsh-skin play data with Xela signals formatted as images.

datasets.name: Sparsh-X dataset (Allegro part)
datasets.title: Tactile Beyond Pixels: Multisensory Touch Representations for Robot Manipulation
datasets.summary: Allegro hand on a Franka Panda with four Digit 360 fingertips dipping into trays of LEGO bricks and marbles, released as raw ROS 2 MCAP bags (tactile images, contact audio, IMU, pressure, joint states, RealSense RGB-D); the handheld-picker part of the Sparsh-X set is excluded.
datasets.hand: Allegro Hand (16 DoF) on Franka Panda

sensor.note: Per Digit 360 (topics /d360_0 .. /d360_3) in the MCAP: image_raw/compressed and tactile_image, both 1280x720 JPEG at 30 Hz; pressure_topic (pressure ~93,600-93,900, Pa by range, + temperature) at 200 Hz; pressure_ap_topic (2 x 25 uint16 per message) at ~910 msg/s; mic_0 and mic_1 (512 float32 samples per message, 48 kHz); imu_raw_topic (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, linear acceleration, ~390 Hz each) and imu_quat_topic (~100 Hz); ght_topic (gas, humidity, temperature) at ~5 Hz; binary_tactile_array (16 float32, all zero in the checked messages).

scale.text: Paper: 4.5 of the 18.6 h Sparsh-X set come from the Allegro hand (8 sequences of ~8.5 min, four sensors each). Release: one 30.4 GB archive of MCAP bags; its first bag (lego_dip, 13.1 GB) covers 100 s

datasets.access: Hugging Face facebook/sparsh-x-dataset, ungated: 5 tar.gz archives (89.5 GB). The Allegro part is d360/20240830-fre-metahand.tar.gz (30.4 GB, raw MCAP bags) plus d360/20240601-fre-metahand.tar.gz (2.4 MB, labels only). A tar.gz can only be read from the start.
caveats: The dataset card describes one data.pickle per sequence, but in every archive checked data.pickle is a symlink to an absolute cluster path (/fsx-gum/shared/...). 20240601-fre-metahand.tar.gz (32 sequences: knife cutting, pan stirring, spatula tapping) therefore holds only metadata.yaml/info.yaml files and no sensor data.

20240830-fre-metahand.tar.gz holds raw ROS 2 MCAP bags with uncompressed chunks. Its first member, 1-none/lego_dip.mcap, is 13.1 GB for 100 s (bag_start/bag_end in metadata.yaml), ~124 MB/s, mostly raw RealSense images.

The rest of the 30.4 GB archive was not listed: gzip has no index, so a listing needs the whole download. The repository's SSL config names 5 sequences in this set (dip lego x 2, dip marble, pour water bottle x 2); whether all of the paper's 8 Allegro sequences of ~8.5 min are released is not confirmed.
The paper's 18.6 h include 14.1 h from a handheld two-finger picker (d360/2024*-trash_picker archives, 59 GB); this entry covers only the Allegro hand.
The 4.5 h Allegro figure matches sensor-hours (8 sequences x 8.5 min x 4 sensors = 4.5 h), i.e. about 1.1 h of recording time; the paper does not say which it counts.
No episode index file: labels (object, action, surface, bag start/end) are in metadata.yaml next to each dangling data.pickle.
tf_static lists ReSkin links on the Allegro phalanges and palm, but no ReSkin topic appears in the first 2.4 s of lego_dip.mcap. The compressed depth topics carry empty images (88-byte messages).

tracking.system: Allegro 16 joint positions, velocities and efforts (/allegroHand/joint_states, ~336 Hz) + /allegroHand/joint_cmd (~34 Hz)

tracking.note: /joint_states merges arm and hand (23 joints, ~71 Hz)
with /teleop_tool_desired_joint_pose (14 values) these suggest teleoperation; the paper only says the hand 'performs random motions'

other: Digit 360 contact microphones, 2 per sensor, 48 kHz
Digit 360 gas, humidity and temperature
RealSense infrared stereo pair and camera_info/extrinsics
Allegro joint temperatures and status
URDF (/robot_description) and tf

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/facebook/sparsh-x-dataset d360/20240601-fre-metahand.tar.gz and d360/20241009-fre-trash_picker.tar.gz (downloaded whole, 2.4 MB and 0.6 MB)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/facebook/sparsh-x-dataset d360/20240830-fre-metahand.tar.gz bytes 0-80,000,000 (127 MB of lego_dip.mcap decoded: schemas, channels, messages) and the gzip trailer of three archives
unconfirmed: Rates are message rates measured over the first 2.4 s of lego_dip.mcap (D360 topics) or its first 0.7 s (RealSense), not stated rates; the card states 30 Hz images, 400 Hz IMU, 48 kHz microphones and 200 Hz pressure.
pressure_topic unit not stated (values 93,600-93,900, Pa by range); the GHT sensor reads 101,827 for ambient pressure.
hours=4.5 is the paper's figure 8 value for the Allegro hand; the interpretation as sensor-hours is ours (8 x 8.5 min x 4 = 272 min = 4.5 h).

Release extent: if every bag in 20240830-fre-metahand.tar.gz records like lego_dip (~124 MB/s, compression to ~63% in the gzip stream), the 30.4 GB archive holds about 6-7 min of recording. Not checked.

The 20240601 'metahand' sequences (knife, pan, spatula) are labelled tool metahand_v1 with allegro_joint and franka_joint true in info.yaml, i.e. Allegro hand on Franka holding tools; none of their sensor data is in the release.
Camera model and mount are not stated; topic names say RealSense.

used_by.name: Sparsh-X, CoRL 2025 (arXiv 2506.14754)
used_by.note: The Allegro part (4.5 of the 18.6 h pretraining set, dipping into trays of LEGO bricks and marbles) is this catalog entry.

datasets.name: 3dtacdex
datasets.title: Canonical Representation and Force-Based Pretraining of 3D Tactile for Dexterous Visuo-Tactile Policy Learning
datasets.summary: Right LEAP hand on a JAKA MiniCobo arm with 8 PaXini 3-axis pads (15 taxels each, thumb to ring fingertips and pulps), teleoperated through HaMeR + DexPilot for box opening, cap flipping, assembly and play data, with 2 fixed RGB-D views at 5 Hz.
datasets.hand: LEAP Hand (16 DoF, right) on a JAKA MiniCobo 6-DoF arm

sensor.note: data/right_tactile_data_fingers (T, 8, 15, 3) float64: 8 pads x 15 taxels x 3-axis force, raw uncalibrated readings (whole numbers; -100 to 105 over all 47,124 frames). Pad order thumb_tip, thumb_pulp, index_tip, index_pulp, middle_tip, middle_pulp, ring_tip, ring_pulp; tips PX6AX-GEN1-DP-S2716, pulps PX6AX-GEN1-IP-S2516 (3x5 taxels each per the paper). No little finger on the LEAP hand, no palm pads.
sensor.model: PX-6AX GEN1 (PX6AX-GEN1-DP-S2716 fingertip, PX6AX-GEN1-IP-S2516 finger pulp)

scale.text: 47,124 frames at 5 Hz (~2.6 h), 328 continuous segments from 283 source trajectories, 4 task stores (assembly 22,069 / flip 12,570 / play_data 8,814 / openbox 3,671 frames)

datasets.access: Hugging Face kingchou007/3dtacdex, ungated: one ZIP64 archive (ZIP_STORED) per task holding a Zarr v2 store, 174 GB in total; single arrays and frames can be range-read from the archives.
caveats: License not stated: the card says 'final release version and license are not yet specified' and that no license is inferred from public availability.
Public review draft for Open-X-Tactile (OXT); official acceptance pending. Uploaded by a paper co-author (kingchou007, Jinzhou Li per the card contact).
5 Hz: demonstrations were recorded at the policy rate (paper: collection and inference at 5 Hz).
Tactile values are uncalibrated; axis signs, physical slot placement and camera conventions still need collection-owner confirmation (card).
openbox: the four middle- and ring-finger pads read zero in every frame; the owner states this is expected.
25,846 frames carry a source 'nouse' label whose training meaning is not documented; play_data mixes train (frames 0-7,705) and test (7,706-8,813), split by data/source_split.
No success labels; instructions are coarse labels derived from directory names. The one-trajectory reorient task (195 frames) was removed.
RGB is stored per frame as lossless Zarr chunks (~1.9 MB main + ~1.0 MB secondary per frame); a 20 s segment costs ~290 MB for both views.

cameras.note: data/camera_main_rgb + raw/camera_1_depth_image (uint16, unit not stated). The paper names an Intel RealSense D415 mounted diagonally to the robot as the policy camera.
data/camera_secondary_rgb + raw/camera_2_depth_image; card: 'additional fixed external camera'. The paper's second camera is a D415 for HaMeR hand tracking; whether this is it is not stated.

tracking.system: LEAP Hand 16 joints (source radians) + commanded joints, velocities, efforts in raw/
tracking.note: joint-to-URDF mapping in OXT_Submission_3dtacdex/mapping_notes.json

tracking.system: JAKA MiniCobo 6 joints + Link_6 flange pose in robot base (m + rotation vector)
tracking.note: not a calibrated palm pose

tracking.system: HaMeR on an Intel RealSense D415 + DexPilot retargeting
tracking.note: teleoperation (paper Sec. III); operator hand pose not released

other: source lineage per frame (record SHA256, source episode id, frame index, version group, train/test split)
coarse English sub-task instruction per frame

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.17549 (Sec. III robot system, Sec. V tasks)
https://huggingface.co/datasets/kingchou007/3dtacdex (README.md, API info, file tree, QUALITY_REPORT.md, CHANGELOG.md, OXT_COMPLIANCE.md)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/kingchou007/3dtacdex openbox/openbox.zarr.zip (ZIP central directory; every .zarray/.zattrs; data/timestamps, meta/episode_ends, data/right_tactile_data_fingers, data/sub_task_instruction chunks)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/kingchou007/3dtacdex {openbox,flip,play_data,assembly}.zarr.zip (all chunks of timestamps, episode_ends, right_tactile_data_fingers, sub_task_instruction, source_split, source_group)
unconfirmed: hours = 2.6 derived: 47,124 frames x 0.2 s (timestamps step 0.200 s, checked in the openbox, flip, play_data and assembly stores).
episodes = 328 counts meta/episode_ends segments; the card says they come from 283 source trajectories and are 'not 328 independent human demonstrations'.
Coverage: pulp pads sit on the LEAP 'dip' link (middle phalanx) per mapping_notes.json, so tip + phalanx.

Tactile principle not stated by the card or the paper; the paper says each taxel measures a 3-axis force. The catalog's hardware entry paxini_px6ax lists PX-6AX as magnetic (Hall array) for GEN3/GEN4; this release uses GEN1.
Camera models of the released views not stated in the release; RGB sizes from the .zarray shapes (1280x720 and 1024x768).
Depth unit not stated ('original source values; per-camera calibration not asserted').
Card contact kingchou007@gmail.com; author name Jinzhou Li is inferred from the handle and the author list, not stated.

zh.note: Dataset card and metadata.json give the institution as '北京大学（Peking University）'; QUALITY_REPORT.md is in Chinese.

used_by.name: 3DTacDex, ICRA 2025 (arXiv 2409.17549)
used_by.note: Encoder pretraining on the authors' play data and diffusion-policy training on demonstrations for 4 tasks (open box, reorientation, flip, assembly), 78% average success. The paper gives no demonstration counts; the catalog release holds 8,814 play frames at 5 Hz plus open-box, flip and assembly demos.

used_by.name: AdapTac-Dex, IROS 2025 (arXiv 2505.13982)
used_by.note: Uses the pretrained 3DTacDex tactile encoder (paper cites Wu et al. 2024); 3DTacDex-P is also a baseline (40% average success against 93%).

used_by.name: T-Dex, CoRL 2023 (arXiv 2303.12076)
used_by.note: Third-party: the 3DTacDex paper (arXiv 2409.17549, Table I) trains a T-Dex-style baseline (tactile as 2D images, BYOL pretraining) on its own play data inside the same diffusion policy; 63% average success over 4 tasks against 78% for 3DTacDex.

datasets.name: TachinTactileGlove-Demo01
datasets.title: TachinTactileGlove-Demo01
datasets.summary: Bimanual Tachin tactile gloves (880 taxels per hand, 15 pads, pressure plus x/y tangential fields) recorded with a head-mounted fisheye RGB camera on a desk in 11 motion categories, with 21-joint hand tracks and SLAM camera poses estimated from the video.
datasets.hand: Tachin tactile glove x 2

sensor.note: 15 pads per hand (keys tactile_0-5, 7-9, 11-13, 15, 16, 18): thumb tip 16x10, thumb mid 4x8, thumb base 13x8; index, middle and ring 9x8 + 3x8 + 4x8; pinky 9x8 + 3x8; palm 13x8 = 880 values. Each pad also has tf_tactile_x and tf_tactile_y fields of the same shape (card: 'local X/Y transform'; launch press: tangential force). Processed LeRobot files hold the three fields per frame at 30 fps (resampled to the video frames); raw npz files keep the glove's own timestamps at about 55.6 Hz (median step 18 ms over WiFi, sensor class 'Wifi32'). Units not stated; pressure values 0 to about 4.2 in the checked files.

scale.text: 102 processed segments (54,237 frames at 30 fps, 30.1 min) cut from 31 of 34 raw sessions (37.9 min of video), 11 motion categories, 31 task recordings; card says about 1 h

datasets.access: Hugging Face Tachintech/TachinTactileGlove-Demo01, ungated, 4.1 GB: 102 per-segment LeRobot v3 ZIPs (5-119 MB each) under Processed/<category>/ and 34 raw sessions under Origin/.
caveats: Small: 102 segments of 1.5-62.5 s (median 12.8 s) recorded on one day (2026-07-10, 16:26-17:38) at one desk, with two glove pairs (two MAC address pairs) and overlapping session times, so likely two stations; the number of subjects is not stated.

Hand pose and camera pose are estimated from the egocentric video (21 OpenPose-style joints, 16 joint rotation matrices per hand, SLAM camera trajectory); there is no hand-tracking hardware. Joints are in the camera frame at raw SLAM scale.

Task names and descriptions (meta/segment_info.json) are in Chinese only; folder names give 11 English motion categories (Fold, Grasp, Plug&Unplug, Pour, Press, Push&Pull, Scroll, Squeeze, Tighten a screw, Twist the bottle cap, Wipe). Launch press describes the release as covering 20 task categories.
Tactile units are not stated. Launch press says calibrated tactile data are provided; the release has no unit or calibration file.
Raw videos are HEVC although the raw-format guide says H.264; processed segment videos are H.264.

Three raw sessions (20260710_163343_778, 164007_606, 165853_253) have no processed segment; two raw-session video clocks differ by 12.4 s between meta_data.json mp4_start_time and video_ntp_time.csv for one glove pair.

Derived release: MIT-Media-Lab/tachin-annotations-v1 (CC BY-NC 4.0) re-cuts the 102 segments into 2,422 per-hand episodes with MANO fits from MIT-Media-Lab/tachin-vitra-precut-mano-v1 (GPL-3.0), which pins this dataset at revision 2eb0e45e.

tracking.system: hand tracking from the egocentric video (algorithm not named)
tracking.note: observation.joints 2 x 21 x 3 and rotmats 2 x 16 x 3 x 3 per frame, with per-hand validity and confidence

tracking.system: same hand tracker; camera trajectory from monocular SLAM on the fisheye video
tracking.note: slam_pose (7,) and R/t world-to-camera per frame; slam_scale in meta/worldpose_static.json; sparse keyframe disparity maps in meta/slam_keyframes.npz

other: per-pad x/y tangential fields (tf_tactile_x/y)
Chinese task name and description per segment
fisheye intrinsics and distortion per segment
raw glove streams with acquisition-side Unix timestamps

sources: Processed/Plug&Unplug/task-63-segment-002.zip (whole file) and meta/info.json, meta_data.json, segment_info.json, stats.json of the other zips by range reads
Origin/customized_glove_无_20260710_162622_504_0/ (all files), plus video_ntp_time.csv and meta_data.json of all 34 raw sessions
unconfirmed: hours=0.5 and frames=54,237 summed from meta/info.json total_frames of the 102 processed ZIPs (30 fps). Raw sessions: 68,173 video frames in the 34 video_ntp_time.csv files = 37.9 min. The card's 'approximately one hour' counts neither figure exactly.

tasks=11 is the number of category folders; the folders hold 31 task ids (task-38 to task-71), each matched by start time to one raw session. Launch press (科技日报 2026-08-21): '包含抓取、折叠、装配、插拔、倾倒、按压、滚动、挤压、旋转、擦拭等20类触觉丰富的操作任务' [contains 20 categories of touch-rich tasks such as grasping, folding, assembly, plug/unplug, pouring, pressing, rolling, squeezing, rotating and wiping]. The release has 11.

Raw tactile rate 55.6 Hz is the median step in one raw session (933 left / 951 right samples over 19.9 s; steps 0-175 ms). Processed tactile_timestamp steps are exactly 1/30 s and values are fractional between raw levels, so the processed tactile is interpolated onto video frames; the method is not stated (the MIT derived card says interpolated without crossing gaps above 100 ms).

Camera mount 'head' and scene type 'lab' are read from two video frames (downward view of a white desk with the wearer's cap at the frame edge); the card says only 'ego-view camera'. Camera model not stated; worldpose_static.json gives camera_model 'fisheye' with 4 distortion coefficients.
Two glove pairs: left/right MACs 8c:8c:29:55:73:b0 / 8c:8c:29:56:4c:68 (44 segments) and d4:8c:49:98:cb:b4 / 8c:8c:29:55:fe:ac (58 segments); raw sessions of the two pairs overlap in time.

Same glove family as the catalog's TouchScale entry (hardware tachin_glove): identical 15-pad layout and 880 values per hand. The glove model name TachinGlove comes from the launch press, not from the card.

zzzqzzz/ego_2_tianji (no license, 1,006 episodes, 4.0 h) retargets a Tachin glove dataset it calls '10h' to a ZYHand robot; its upstream could not be traced to this release, so it is not listed as a user.
Units of tf_tactile_x/y not stated; values -1.34 to 1.04 in the checked raw session.

The video shows brown or orange outer gloves with a module on the back of the hand; segment descriptions call them '棕色工作手套' [brown work gloves] or '橙色手套' [orange gloves]. Whether the tactile glove is worn under an outer glove is not stated.

zh.note: English dataset name is the publisher's. Format guides come in English and Chinese (RAW_UPLOAD_DATA_CN.md, LEROBOT_DATASET_CN.md); per-segment task names and descriptions are Chinese only. Launch press calls the release 首批全手触觉具身数据集 [first batch of whole-hand tactile embodied data]; full company name in press: 途见科技（北京）有限公司.

datasets.name: Fixed Viewpoint Tactile Dataset
datasets.title: Fixed Viewpoint Tactile Dataset
datasets.summary: One Tachin tactile glove (20 pads, 932 taxels) on a human hand, recorded by a static RGB-D camera and a fixed motion-capture setup tracking 20 hand points, over 160 episodes of 4 tabletop tasks (whiteboard wiping, peg-in-hole, pliers, cylinder lift).
datasets.hand: Tachin tactile glove x 1 (one hand)

sensor.note: 20 pads (tactile_0 to tactile_19, flattened per pad; 2-D shapes in meta/info.json tactile_2d_shapes): thumb tip 16x10, mid 4x8, base 6x15; index, middle and ring tip 9x8, mid 3x8, base 4x8, palm-side joint 3x4; pinky tip 9x8, mid 3x8, base 4x8, palm-side joint 3x4; palm 15x6. Pad roles from the publisher's visualize_dataset.py labels. Units not stated; values 0 to 2.6 in data file 0 with small per-episode offsets (the publisher's viewer subtracts the mean of the first 10 frames).

scale.text: 160 episodes, 59,158 frames at 20 fps (49 min), 4 tasks: peg-in-hole 82, whiteboard wiping 62, pliers 10, cylinder lift 6

datasets.access: Hugging Face Tachintech/Fixed_Viewpoint_Tactile_Dataset, ungated, 3.8 GB LeRobot v3.0 (50 data parquet files, 50 RGB and 50 depth mp4 files).
caveats: One hand only; the card does not say which, and the checked video shows a single gloved hand.

Hand tracking is 20 points with a position and a quaternion each from a 'fixed-position motion-capture device' (固定机位动捕设备); the system, marker set and units are not named. Missing samples are stored as all-zero frames (0-1.2% of frames per checked episode).
Depth video is stored as 3-channel MPEG-4 Part 2 (lossy) with banding in the decoded frame; the depth encoding and units are not documented. RGB video is also MPEG-4 Part 2, not H.264.
Tactile units are not stated; meta/info.json declares float32 but the parquet stores float64.
Card text is in Chinese; the title, task strings and field names are English.
Task balance is uneven: the cylinder-lift episodes (6) show little touch (4 of 6 checked peak below 2 summed units above baseline).

tracking.note: observation_motion_positions (20 x 3) and observation_motion_quaternions (20 x 4, w-first in the publisher's viewer) per frame; the viewer labels them '20 markers, 5 fingers'

other: English task string per episode
publisher web viewer (visualize_dataset.py) with pad layout and skeleton

sources: data/chunk-000/file-0000, 0022, 0023, 0024, 0025, 0030.parquet (whole files); videos/observation.images.color/chunk-000/file-0000.mp4 (whole); videos/observation.images.depth/chunk-000/file-0000.mp4 (one frame via ffmpeg range reads)
unconfirmed: hours=0.82 derived: 59,158 frames / 20 fps.

taxels_per_hand=932 summed from meta/info.json tactile_2d_shapes (20 pads). The Demo01 release of the same maker has 880 values in 15 pads; this glove adds four 3x4 palm-side pads, a third pinky pad, and uses 6x15 / 15x6 shapes for thumb base and palm.
Glove on a human hand confirmed from RGB frames of episode 1 (gloved hand with a mount on the back, sweater sleeve). Which hand is not stated.
