datasets.name: TactAlign
datasets.title: TactAlign: Human-to-Robot Policy Transfer via Tactile Alignment
datasets.summary: Unpaired pivoting and insertion demonstrations from a human wearing the OSMO magnetic tactile glove (index-fingertip 3-axis signal) and from an Allegro hand with XELA 30-taxel fingertip sensors on a Franka arm, released as fingertip tactile, fingertip/wrist state, estimated object pose and actions at 10 Hz.
datasets.hand: Human hand in the OSMO tactile glove; Wonik Allegro Hand (16 DoF) with XELA fingertip sensors on a Franka Emika Panda

sensor.note: Released per frame, one fingertip per modality. Human: observation/tactile (3, 1, 3) = the last 3 samples of one 3-axis OSMO reading on the index fingertip (finger column 'index' in every row), signed, near 0 at rest, peaks of ~200-1,500. Robot: observation/tactile (10, 30, 3) = 10 consecutive XELA samples (100 Hz) of one 30-taxel fingertip, 3 axes each. Frames are 0.1 s apart. Paper: glove recorded at 30 fps, XELA at 100 fps; glove baseline removed per trajectory, XELA baseline recorded per session. No force units.
sensor.maker: Meta FAIR (OSMO glove); XELA Robotics (robot fingertips)
sensor.model: OSMO tactile glove; XELA uSkin fingertip sensors (30 taxels each)

scale.text: Release: 210 human glove demonstrations (37,740 frames @10 Hz, ~63 min; pivoting 103 + insertion 98 + 9 val) and 104 robot episodes in the XELA encoder repo (9,876 frames, ~16.5 min, incl. one 300 s play episode); the two downstream robot repos (100 episodes) repeat the encoder repo's pivoting and insertion episodes. Paper: 200 human + 100 robot alignment demos, 140-160 human and 50 robot demos per co-training task (pivoting, insertion, lid closing), 20 human light-bulb demos

datasets.access: Four ungated Hugging Face repos by the first author (youngw/tactile_align_encoder_pretrain_glove, _encoder_pretrain_xela, _downstream_insertion, _downstream_pivoting; 204 MB, Hugging Face datasets Arrow files with train/val splits), with no dataset card and no link from the paper or project page; the project page lists code as 'Coming Soon' and its data link is commented out.
caveats: Only pivoting and insertion are released; lid closing, light-bulb screwing (Manus glove + OSMO), the human-only-object demos, the force-labelled F/T dataset, play data for the glove, and all camera images are not in the repos.

One fingertip per sample: the glove repo carries only the index fingertip (one 3-axis reading), the robot repos one 30-taxel XELA fingertip; which Allegro finger is not stated (the paper's pivoting policy uses the index fingertip).

No images or depth: the RealSense D455 frames used for WiLoR hand pose and FoundationPose object pose are not released; observation/state and observation/object_pose are those estimates (human) or proprioception (robot).
No dataset card, README or license on any of the four repos; the arXiv paper is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the project page CC BY-SA 4.0, neither covers the data.

Tactile values are baseline-subtracted magnetic readings without units; the paper takes the absolute value of the glove signal because the OSMO skin flips sign by quadrant, but the release keeps signed values.
Robot insertion episodes are 2.6-9.3 s and pivoting 5-15.6 s; robot demonstrations are kinesthetic teaching, not teleoperation.
The glove repo's metadata/info.json says fps 30 while its timestamps step by 0.1 s.

episodes=314 = 210 glove (201 train + 9 val) + 104 XELA encoder episodes (99 + 5); frames=47,616 = 37,740 + 9,876; hours=1.32 at the 0.1 s frame step. The downstream repos (insertion 49 + 3, pivoting 46 + 2 episodes) are left out because their episodes have the same lengths and peak values as encoder-repo episodes (e.g. downstream pivoting 27 = encoder 61, 156 frames, peak 2,230), i.e. they look like the same demonstrations.

The (3, 1, 3) glove array is a 3-step history window: slice i+1 of each row equals slice i of the next row. The (10, 30, 3) XELA array holds 10 distinct consecutive samples per frame (no overlap between rows), consistent with 100 fps XELA in 0.1 s frames.
XELA model: 30 taxels per fingertip matches XELA's curved Allegro fingertip (uSCu ALHA, 30 points); the paper says only 'Xela sensors mounted on the Allegro Hand fingertips'.
The paper's glove has 'three-axis magnetic tactile signals at the fingertips'; the OSMO glove has 12 taxels (5 fingertips + palm), but only the index fingertip is released.

objects: the alignment set uses one shared object per task (paper: Cheez-It box for pivoting, an adapter for insertion); whether the glove repo also holds human-only objects is not stated. Subjects not stated.
scenes=1: one Franka tabletop setup; not stated as a count.

datasets.name: UVTA
datasets.title: Unified Visual-Tactile-Action Modeling from Human Demonstrations for Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Right-hand demonstrations of 5 contact-rich tasks from people wearing a passive 22-DoF exoskeleton glove with fingertip FSR arrays (5,000) and from a teleoperated Sharpa Wave hand on a Sharpa North robot (749), released as 20 fingertip-region touch values, wrist fisheye video and 22 joint angles at 30 Hz.
datasets.hand: Human right hand in a passive 22-DoF exoskeleton glove (fingertip FSR arrays); Sharpa Wave (22 DoF), right hand of a fixed-base Sharpa North

sensor.note: Released field tactile (T, 20) float32 for both embodiments: 5 fingertips (thumb, index, middle, ring, little) x 4 regions (A tip = 5 taxels, B side = 3, C middle = 9, D side = 3), each the mean of its taxels. Human: FSR array of 20 taxels per fingertip read from a 240-value glove payload (blocks 0-19, 40-59, 80-99, 120-139, 160-179), raw counts (region means up to ~1,700 in the checked episodes). Robot: Sharpa Wave fingertip deformation maps (240x240 grayscale) summed per glove-taxel region by a fixed pixel-to-taxel map, then averaged per region (VTPM); values up to ~140,000 in the checked episodes. Raw taxels, Sharpa tactile images, deformation maps and the fingertip force magnitudes named in the metadata are not released. The paper subtracts a per-recording baseline (human: mean of first 5 frames; robot: first frame).
sensor.maker: not stated (FSR exoskeleton glove); robot: Sharpa
sensor.model: FSR fingertip arrays on a passive 22-DoF exoskeleton glove; robot: Sharpa Wave fingertip tactile sensor

scale.text: 5,749 episodes over 5 tasks: 5,000 human (1,000 per task) + 749 robot (150 per task, 149 for flip_book); ~19.7 h at 30 Hz (16.3 h human, 3.4 h robot; derived from file counts); 482 GB

datasets.access: Hugging Face Chopper233/UVTA, ungated, 28 tar shards (5-22 GB each, 482 GB in total) of Zarr v2 episode stores, one set of shards per task and embodiment.
caveats: Touch is released only as 20 pooled values per frame (4 regions per fingertip); raw glove taxels, Sharpa tactile images, deformation maps and fingertip forces are not in the release.

Robot touch is derived from Sharpa Wave deformation maps by a fixed pixel-to-glove-taxel map (VTPM), so robot values (up to ~140,000) and human FSR counts (up to ~1,700 in the checked episodes) are on different scales; neither is in physical units.
Right hand only: the robot has two Sharpa Wave hands, but only the right arm, right hand and right wrist camera are released. Fingertips only, no phalanx or palm sensing.
Robot demonstrations use one fixed scene per task (layout, start pose, table height); human demonstrations vary objects, backgrounds and glove colour (black or white).
Human actions are derived: hand_action and pose_action are the next frame's joint angles and wrist pose.
No per-frame timestamps and no object, scene or operator labels; 30 Hz is the paper's resampling rate. The robot metadata names a head stereo camera that is not released.
Per-frame RGB is stored as blosc-lz4 Zarr chunks inside large tar shards with no per-episode byte offsets; fetching one episode means walking the tar headers or streaming the shard from its start.
Many episodes are shorter than 10 s (mean 7.7 s for robot switch, 8.7 s for human flip_book, 9.1 s for human switch).

tracking.system: passive 22-DoF linkage exoskeleton (carbon-fibre links, dorsal mount, joint encoders)
tracking.note: human; encoder FK -> fingertip poses in the Sharpa Wave palm frame -> constrained IK to the 22 Sharpa Wave joint angles, released as proprioception

tracking.system: HTC VIVE Tracker 3.0 x 2 (one fixed to the table as reference, one on the wrist via a 3D-printed adapter)
tracking.note: human; released as pose (xyz + rotation vector) in the robot base frame after calibration

tracking.system: Sharpa Wave right-hand joint angles (22) and commanded targets
tracking.note: robot

tracking.system: Sharpa North right-arm forward kinematics (arm joints + 5 torso motors)
tracking.note: robot; observed and commanded end-effector pose
robot demonstrations are teleoperated; the teleoperation device is not stated

other: commanded wrist pose and 22 hand joint targets (robot: teleop commands; human: next-frame state)

sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34182 (abstract page and PDF v2, incl. Appendix I-IV)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/Chopper233/UVTA switch/robot-00000.tar episode_0 and switch/human-00000.tar episode_0 (all files: .zattrs, rgb, tactile, proprioception, hand_action, pose, pose_action)
https://huggingface.co/datasets/Chopper233/UVTA .zattrs and tactile arrays of 37 more episodes read by tar-header range reads (all 5 tasks, both embodiments)
https://github.com/uni-vta/UVTA (README.md, LICENSE, configs/flip_book.yaml, deform_to_human/fsr_region.py, deform_to_taxel.py, core.py, glove_sharpa_mapping/out/*right.json)
https://huggingface.co/datasets/Sharpa-Robotics/SharpaDex-v1.0 (README.md, season folder names of all 59 tasks) for the overlap check

Mean episode length by task (human / robot): flip_book 8.7 / 9.7 s, light_bulb 13.6 / 31.3 s, switch 9.1 / 7.7 s, ball 10.2 / 12.6 s, tube 17.1 / 20.1 s.

taxels_per_hand = 100 from the release metadata (fsr_layout: 20 taxels per finger at glove payload blocks 0-19 ... 160-179) and deform_to_human/fsr_region.py; the paper describes each fingertip FSR array as 'four sensing regions, each with an active area of 15 x 15 mm2', which matches the 4 pooled regions. The glove payload has 240 values; whether the other 140 positions carry sensors is not stated (the paper says sensing is fingertip-only).
Glove maker, FSR model, native glove sampling rate and force range are not stated; a code comment in deform_to_human/core.py refers to a '~0..4095 glove scale' (12-bit ADC, inferred).
Robot platform name 'Sharpa North' (fixed base, two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands) is from the paper; the release metadata names URDF north_poc2_2 and station POC22002 in the source paths.
Pose xyz unit not stated (values 0.15-1.1, consistent with metres); joint-angle unit not stated (range about -0.4 to 1.25, consistent with radians).
Wrist camera model and native resolution not stated; released frames are 480x384 RGB (resize_hw [384, 480]). The decoded robot and human frames are fisheye views with near-neutral colour.
Collection dates from source file paths in the episode metadata: human 2026-07-05 to 2026-08-21, robot 2026-07-08 to 2026-08-22 (shard-first and probed episodes only).
Human B_side regions were zero for the whole switch human episode_0 but active in flip_book human episode_3; no dead region is claimed.
subjects not stated: human source folders carry names such as ZZH-0705, tablecloth-170, light-100, ball_1_ego, dropper_ego, which are not documented.

Overlap with SharpaDex v1.0: its 495 seasons span 2026-03 to 2026-07-07 on stations POC22002/07/18/21/27/32/48/50/54/61/65 (POC22002 only in deal_playing_cards, 2026-07-01 to 07-03); the UVTA robot seasons seen (POC22002, 2026-07-08 to 08-22) are not among them, and SharpaDex is bimanual LeRobot with 60-D fingertip wrench and tactile videos. Related task themes exist (SharpaDex turn_book_pages, transfer_liquid_with_dropper). Checked by season names of 6 robot shard-first episodes and 20 probed robot episodes, not every UVTA episode.

Overlap with T-Rex (catalog trex): different platform (Dexmate Vega-1 + two Sharpa Wave, robot_type dexmate_vega1_and_sharpa_wave), format (LeRobot v3) and tasks. UVTA uses the pretrained T-Rex model as a baseline post-trained on UVTA robot demos; the paper does not train on the T-Rex dataset or any other public dataset.

datasets.summary: Tencent's 3-finger TRX-Hand with a 620-taxel piezoresistive skin on fingers and palm holds one of 4 released objects while an ABB arm moves it through workspace poses; each snapshot pairs the activated-taxel positions with RGB-D, finger poses and Vicon object pose (plus a MuJoCo/Blender simulated split).
datasets.hand: TRX-Hand (Tencent Robotics X, 3 fingers, 8 DoF) on an ABB arm; the simulated split uses a MuJoCo model of the same hand

sensor.note: Released touch is not per-taxel pressure. Each snapshot has touch_point_cloud.ply: x, y, z (float64, m) of the activated taxels in the hand frame, 5-53 points per real sample (median 11-31 per object). Paper: sensors respond above 250 Hz with a non-linear response to normal force; the released data are single snapshots about 1-2 s apart.
sensor.model: TRX-Hand whole-hand tactile skin (curved piezoresistive arrays)

scale.text: Released real split: 37,294 snapshots of 4 objects in 41 sessions (paper: 100,000 snapshots of 10 objects); simulated split: 57,500 TRX-Hand grasps of 23 objects x 16 rendered views (paper: 2M samples including an Allegro hand)

caveats: Touch is released only as positions of activated taxels (touch_point_cloud.ply). No per-taxel pressure values, taxel IDs or taxel layout file are in the release.

Real data are snapshots, not continuous recordings: each object was grasped in about 10 sessions of roughly 950 snapshots taken 1-2 s apart while the arm moved through 125 positions x 8 hand rotations. The object stays in one grasp; there is no in-hand manipulation.
Only 4 of the paper's 10 real objects are released (folders 5, 7, 900, 904); names are not given in the release.
The simulated split contains only the TRX-Hand. No data from the 679-taxel Allegro skin described in the paper (simulated or real) is released.
No code, object meshes or marker-fixture models are in the release or linked from the project page (the paper says the fixtures are on the website; not found).
Simulated touch is a MuJoCo contact model (activated sensor positions), not measured data.

Sessions: snapshot folder names are MMDDHHMMSS time stamps (year not encoded). Gaps over 60 s split them into 10 / 11 / 10 / 10 sessions of up to 964 snapshots, 1-2 s apart, recorded on 2024-03-03 to 03-12 (year assumed from the paper date). The paper describes 10 variations per object over 1,000 poses; the session-to-variation match is inferred.
Activated taxels per real snapshot (5-53, medians 31 / 19 / 27 / 11) derived from PLY file sizes (24 bytes per float64 vertex after a 144-145 byte header); one file opened to confirm (31 vertices).

Simulated split: 23 objects x 2,500 grasps = 57,500 grasps; each sample folder has 16 views (rgb/*.jpg, depth/*.png, mask/*.png). Counted in syn_trx_05.zip; the other 22 zips assumed to match. Real depth.png is 16-bit with values 579-827 in the opened sample (mm by range; the real camera.json has no depth_scale, the simulated one has depth_scale 1.0). Only 19,089 of 256,000 pixels are non-zero in that sample, so the depth appears cropped to the hand-object region.

datasets.access: Project page fact-1-0.github.io shows 'Data (Coming Soon)' and 'Code (Coming Soon)' (2026-10-27); the paper has no release, license or dataset URL statement.
caveats: Not released: the numbers come from the paper and project page, and no file was seen.

Hand pose is estimated from video (ViTPose keypoints and HaMeR MANO meshes on the left stereo view, scaled with stereo depth), refined with the glove bend sensors and IMU when the hand is occluded; no motion capture.
Fingertip and palm only: 12 taxels per fingertip, none on the other phalanges.
Task categories are named (deformable manipulation, assembly, storage, other fine manipulation); objects are not counted.

tracking.system: ViTPose hand keypoints and HaMeR MANO meshes on the left stereo view
tracking.note: smoothed and scaled with stereo depth; glove bend sensors and IMU refine finger flexion under occlusion

tracking.system: glove bend sensor, one per finger

tracking.note: orientation only

other: 200 Hz IMU in the head stereo camera and an IMU in each wrist camera

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.19155v1 (dataset section, appendix on the glove and cameras, acknowledgments)
unconfirmed: taxels_per_hand = 120 = 5 x 12 fingertip + 60 palm, summed from the paper's appendix; the layout matches the conductive-fabric glove in the catalog's fusionx_sample release (4x3 per finger, 4x15 palm), but the paper does not name the glove generation.
subjects = 1,000 is the paper's count of demonstrators; whether these are distinct people is not stated.
Who collected the data and where is not stated; the acknowledgments say it was 'collected with the FusionX multimodal data collection system (TouchTronix Robotics, NY, USA)'.
The modality 'egocentric' is the head-mounted stereo pair; 'wrist_rgb' the two 1920x1080 wrist cameras.

used_by.name: FACT, arXiv 2610.19155
used_by.note: About 2,000 h of human demonstrations with TouchTronix glove force; pretraining on the human data without force lowers results on 9 of the 10 tasks (open test-tube cap 80% to 0%; multi-object grasp unchanged at 40%).

datasets.name: TactileLab In-Hand Rotation
datasets.title: TactileLab: Efficient Shear-Sensitive Tactile Simulation for Sim-to-Real Multi-Finger Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.venue: ICRA 2026 Workshop on Dexterity with Multifingered Hands
datasets.summary: 20 real-world rollouts (30 s each at 10 Hz, 6,000 steps) of sim-to-real RL in-hand rotation policies on a palm-up 4-finger hand built from LEAP Hand finger modules, with a TacTip-family marker-based optical sensor on each fingertip; each step holds four raw 224x224 tactile images, 16 joint positions and one fixed external RGB view.
datasets.hand: Custom palm-up 4-finger hand from LEAP Hand finger modules (16 DoF), Bristol Robotics Laboratory

sensor.note: One TacTip-family marker-based optical sensor per fingertip; right_tactile_data_fingertips holds 4 x 224x224x3 raw tactile camera images per step (sensor tag 'TacTipFingertip', type 'image'), stored at the 10 Hz control rate. From the dataset card; files not opened.

scale.text: 20 episodes (10 household objects x 2 policy variants), 300 steps each at 10 Hz, 6,000 steps; one task (counterclockwise in-hand rotation)

datasets.access: Hugging Face dataset Kitval/TactileLab_InHandRotation, not gated; 20 per-episode zarr zips (1.9 GB in total).
caveats: These are rollouts of policies trained in simulation, not teleoperated demonstrations; the card lists no action stream, only joint positions.
Two policy variants per object: 'full' (proprioception + tactile depth + tactile flow) and 'depth' (proprioception + tactile depth); the stored tactile data are the raw camera images either way.
The card notes that in the 'gum' full-policy episode the object wedged on the fingertips after about 22.5 s and the hand barely moves until the end.
Released in the FTP-1 zarr layout of the Open-X-Tactile (OXT) collection; the card defines the keys but no paper with the data was found (TactileLab project page: arXiv and code 'Coming soon').
No license on the card.

tracking.note: right_hand_joints (16, rad)

other: sub_task_instruction: one fixed language instruction per episode

sources: https://yijionglin.github.io/tactilelab/ (project page: authors, PETS-Net, Leap Hand support, 'arXiv Coming soon', 'Code Coming soon')
unconfirmed: hours: 20 episodes x 30 s = 10 min, derived from the card's per-episode length; not stated as a total.

Venue and the two-author list (Lin, Lepora) come from the card's BibTeX; the project page lists six authors and a different title ('TactileLab: Efficient Multimodal Tactile Simulation for Shear-Sensitive Dexterous Sim2Real Robotic Manipulation'). The catalog uses the card's title.
That the rolled-out policies are the project page's PETS-Net is likely but not stated on the card.
Per-episode size of about 95 MB is 1.9 GB / 20; zips not opened.
Publisher account 'Kitval' is not named on the project page; its link to the Lepora lab is from the card's citation only.

datasets.name: ExoBridge
datasets.title: ExoBridge: Learning a Bare Hand to Hand-Worn Exoskeleton Mapping through Human Limb Coupling
datasets.summary: 1,215 paired human demonstrations over 4 tasks in 31 sessions: one hand works bare in front of a fixed RealSense D436 while the other wears a DexUMI-family exoskeleton with 120-taxel tactile arrays on the thumb, index and middle fingertips plus joint encoders; release of the RGB, tactile and encoder data is announced.
datasets.hand: Human hands, bimanual: one bare, the other in a DexUMI-family exoskeleton calibrated to the XHand (12 DoF)

sensor.note: Fingertip tactile arrays with 120 taxels each on the exoskeleton's thumb, index and middle fingers; the model uses every fourth aligned sample (about 5 Hz). Sensor type, maker and native rate not stated. Described in the paper; no files released.

scale.text: 1,215 demonstrations (egg carton opening 245, lid twisting 340, soldering tool orientation 311, USB insertion 319) in 31 sessions; 204,586 aligned steps before subsampling; not released

datasets.access: The paper states the authors 'will release paired RGB recordings, tactile and encoder measurements' with session identifiers, split assignments and evaluation code, and that video distribution will follow participant consent and data-sharing requirements; no link given (arXiv v1, 2026-10-06).
caveats: Not released: the numbers come from the paper, and no file was seen.
Touch is on the exoskeleton hand only, and only at three fingertips; the bare hand that the camera sees carries no sensor.
Hours and subject count are not reported; demonstrations are by 'experts'.
The exoskeleton is calibrated to an XHand on a Franka arm through existing DexUMI-style calibration; no robot data are described as part of the release.

tracking.note: relative encoder motion is one of the model's targets

tracking.system: MediaPipe Hands (bare-hand crop for the model)
tracking.note: used to crop the bare hand, not released as a label

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07692v1 (hardware, dataset, task counts, release statement, results)
unconfirmed: The 120-taxel fingertip arrays match the XHand fingertip modules used in the DexUMI exoskeleton (catalog: dexumi), but the paper does not name the sensor; the hardware link is not set.
Native tactile rate: the model takes every fourth aligned sample for about 5 Hz, which implies about 20 Hz aligned data; 204,586 steps at 20 Hz would be about 2.8 h. Both are derived, not stated.
taxels_per_hand = 3 x 120, summed from the paper.
D436 is the paper's camera name; resolution and frame rate not read.
'hand_pose' here is the exoskeleton's joint encoders, not a MANO or keypoint label.

datasets.name: RSS Dual-Arm Tactile (tube pour)
datasets.title: rss-dual-arm-tactile
datasets.summary: Teleoperated bimanual tube pouring on two UFACTORY xArm6 arms with BrainCo Revo2 hands, each hand wearing a Tujian (Tachin) tactile glove, with a static head camera and a wrist camera per arm: 100 successful trajectories in two batches plus 9 labelled failures, behind a Hugging Face gate.
datasets.hand: BrainCo Revo2 x 2 on UFACTORY xArm6 arms, each covered by a Tujian (Tachin) tactile glove

sensor.note: Card: 'Tujian tactile glove worn on each robot hand'. Taxel count, coverage on the Revo2 hand, rate and file layout are not on the public card; files not opened (gated).

scale.text: Tube pour: 50 successful trajectories (2026-10-05) + 50 (2026-10-21/22), plus 2 and 7 failed or aborted attempts in separate folders; pipette transfer, cap twisting, beaker wiping and cloth folding listed as planned

datasets.access: Hugging Face SingleBicycle/rss-dual-arm-tactile; the files open after agreeing to share Hugging Face contact information (gate listed as manual approval). The repository also holds policy rollout code (rollout_code_20261026).

gate.note: Gate text: 'You need to agree to share your Hugging Face information to access this dataset.' Hugging Face API reports gated: manual.

caveats: No paper or project page; the card refers to an 'RSS project' without a link, and the publisher is a personal account.
Touch comes from gloves pulled over the robot hands, not from the Revo2's own fingertip sensors; the card does not say whether the hands are the tactile Revo2 TOUCH variant.

The card gives 137 GB as the total size, while the Hugging Face API reports 31.2 GB of storage on 2026-10-28; the batch-1 folder is described as a copy of a release in another repository, which is not named.
One task only so far; the failure folders are marked 'Not for training'.
Per-episode streams, rates and the tactile array layout are only in the gated per-folder READMEs, which were not read.

tracking.note: proprioceptive streams not listed on the public card

other: mesh-based two-arm collision guard used during batch 2

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/SingleBicycle/rss-dual-arm-tactile (public card text and gate prompt via the dataset page; repository metadata and top-level listing via the Hugging Face API)
unconfirmed: Tujian = 途见, the Chinese name of Tachin Technology, whose TachinGlove is in the catalog; the card does not give the glove model, so the TachinGlove hardware link rests on the maker name.
episodes = 100 successful trajectories as counted on the card; the 9 failures are not counted.
Teleoperation interface not named; 'teleoperated demonstrations' is from the card summary.
Modalities beyond the three cameras and touch (joint states, actions) are not listed on the public card.
